episode.title: Route shell substitution through reviewable permission decisions with visible warnings
episode.before: At parent commit 5ad5301805ef4aef2abc15596412c54e017c28eb, the permission manager and monitor tool could hard-deny commands containing $(), backticks, <(), or >(). In the permission manager, this happened only when surrounding rules caused full evaluation, so the same substitution could be approvable as a standalone command but denied inside a compound command with an unrelated matching rule. Hard denial also prevented YOLO-mode override. Some substitution shapes outside command AST nodes, and env-prefix substitutions removed by shell-wrapper stripping, could instead be misclassified as read-only and automatically allowed. Execution confirmations had no warnings contract or warning rendering.
episode.after: At a5ec1af301c432622e165ae18dac606e10662113, substitution-bearing agent shell and monitor commands are treated as non-read-only and normally resolve to ask rather than an implicit hard deny, while explicit deny rules retain precedence. Detection covers raw and wrapper-stripped commands, AST substitutions in every statement-node type, and the regex fallback path. Shell and monitor confirmations attach a shared informational warning for substitution, and the CLI renders warning-colored, prefixed text while reserving wrap-aware terminal height so approval options remain visible.
episode.diff: Removed substitution-specific default-deny branches from the permission manager and monitor permission resolver; narrowed the manager's default result to allow or ask; hoisted AST substitution rejection above node-type dispatch; added pre-strip/raw substitution protection to shell permission and fallback read-only checks; introduced shared substitution detection and warning helpers plus an optional warnings field on execution confirmation details; populated warnings in shell and monitor call sites; rendered warnings in the terminal confirmation component with wrapped-row height accounting; and added regression tests for standalone and compound commands, all four substitution syntaxes, wrapper/env-prefix cases, explicit-deny precedence, warning generation/rendering, AST blind spots, and constrained layouts.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit identifies the bug as an inconsistent, non-overridable hard denial of command substitution and states that explicit slash-command shell-injection checking remains out of scope.

The permission manager no longer calls detectCommandSubstitution to return deny from default resolution; default resolution now returns only allow or ask, with AST failures conservatively falling back to ask.

Permission-manager regressions prove that standalone, compound-rule, backtick, input-process, and output-process substitution resolve to ask, while an explicit matching deny rule still resolves to deny.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a shell syntax risk is never denied merely by an inconsistent default branch or silently allowed through classifier gaps: it should require informed approval unless an explicit rule determines otherwise.
when_to_use: A shell-like tool has syntactic-risk checks duplicated across permission layers or sibling tools and equivalent commands receive different decisions depending on unrelated rules.

not_applicable_when: The syntax is prohibited by an explicit non-overridable product or sandbox policy rather than a default permission heuristic.

title: Keep absolute-path conversion usable when canonical resolution encounters a symlink loop
before: At parent commit 4625ebb4b517ce51db0aa7eb92c3fea61243610f, safe_abs_path converted its input solely with Path(res).resolve(). A circular symbolic-link chain therefore raised RuntimeError instead of returning a path. Call sites depended on this helper when constructing coder file paths, normalizing repository-discovered paths, storing the repository working-tree root, converting repository-relative paths, and finding a common root.
after: At commit b2bec25c2c785989d6456cb03321a61f539bcc86, safe_abs_path still prefers Path.resolve(), but catches RuntimeError and OSError and falls back to Path.absolute(), returning the resulting path as a string. A new test constructs a two-link cycle, calls the helper, and asserts that it does not raise and returns an absolute path.
diff: The implementation replaced the unconditional resolve call with a guarded canonical-resolution attempt and a lexical absolute-path fallback. The commit changed aider/utils.py by four added lines and one replaced line, and added tests/basic/test_utils.py with a 15-line circular-symlink regression test. Existing call sites were unchanged and inherit the helper's fallback behavior.

commit.subject: fix: handle symlink loops in safe_abs_path() (#4711)
commit.body_excerpt:
Path.resolve() raises RuntimeError on circular symlinks. Catch
RuntimeError and OSError, fall back to Path.absolute().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

candidate_workflows.name: make-absolute-path-normalization-resilient-to-resolution-failures
candidate_workflows.title: Make absolute-path normalization resilient to symlink-resolution failures
candidate_workflows.description: Harden a shared path-normalization boundary by retaining canonical resolution for ordinary paths while supplying an absolute, non-resolving fallback for circular symlinks and other explicitly covered resolution failures.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure consumers of a shared absolute-path helper receive an absolute path rather than an exception when canonical path resolution cannot complete.
when_to_use: A shared helper currently relies on canonical path resolution and a reproducible circular symbolic-link input causes that boundary to raise.
Downstream consumers require an absolute path, but do not require the fallback result to dereference every symlink.
anti_goals: Do not replace canonical resolution on the successful path.
Do not claim that the fallback identifies the physical filesystem target or validates path existence.
Do not broaden the change to unrelated repository-root discovery or path-containment behavior.
Do not suppress exceptions outside the explicitly selected resolution-failure classes.
not_applicable_when: The caller requires a fully canonical, dereferenced, existing path and cannot safely accept a lexical absolute path.
The failure occurs before the shared normalization boundary is reached.
Returning a non-canonical absolute path would weaken a security or containment check.
inputs: The shared absolute-path normalization boundary
A path input that reproduces the resolution failure
The exception classes emitted by the canonical resolver
Call sites' requirement for absolute versus canonical path semantics
workflow_graph.entry_state: Canonical resolution is the only conversion path, so a circular symlink can prevent the helper from returning any value to its callers.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The helper preserves canonical results when resolution succeeds and returns a lexical absolute-path string when resolution raises RuntimeError or OSError; the circular-symlink regression oracle completes without an exception and observes an absolute result.

steps.condition: Canonical path resolution raises one of the evidence-supported resolution exceptions and downstream semantics permit a non-canonical absolute result.
steps.validation: Exercise a two-link circular symlink and confirm both non-raising behavior and an absolute returned path.

commit.subject: fix(coding-agent): stop loading AGENTS.md twice in nested git worktrees (#7221)
commit.body_excerpt:
Running from a linked worktree nested under its main repo loaded the
project's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md twice. The ancestor walk climbs from cwd to
the filesystem root, so it picked up the worktree's copy and then the main
repo's copy above it, even though both are the same tracked file.

The walk now drops that one duplicate: the main repo root's copy is skipped
when the worktree root has a context file of the same name. Nothing else
changes. The worktree still inherits the main repo's copy when it has none,
directories above the main repo keep loading, and ordinary repos, sibling
worktrees, submodules and bare layouts are untouched.

title: Resolve file edits against one observable absolute workspace target

commit.subject: fix(file-tools): anchor relative-path resolution to absolute base; report resolved path (#35399)
commit.body_excerpt:
Relative paths in write_file/patch could resolve against the agent PROCESS cwd
instead of the terminal's working directory. In a git-worktree session with a
stale TERMINAL_CWD='.' (a relative base), early edits silently landed in the
MAIN checkout, verified there, and reported success — while the agent inspected
the worktree and saw nothing, misreading it as the patch tool no-op'ing.

- _resolve_base_dir(): resolution base is now ALWAYS absolute. A relative
  TERMINAL_CWD is anchored to the process cwd once, deterministically, instead
  of being left to resolve()-time cwd. Live terminal cwd stays authoritative.
- write_file/patch pass the resolved absolute path to the shell FileOps layer
  so the tool layer and shell layer can't disagree about which file is edited.
- Responses now report the absolute resolved_path and files_modified, so a
  wrong-cwd mismatch is visible on the first call.
- _path_resolution_warning(): emits a _warning when a relative path resolves
  OUTSIDE the live terminal cwd (e.g. a worktree session writing into main).

Validation: 11 new unit tests + 43 live E2E assertions (worktree routing,
mid-session cd, V4A patches, divergence warning, absolute paths, cons

episode.title: Resolve file edits against one observable absolute workspace target
episode.before: At parent 0c6e133c0434ec856d4aea2b08f216f36c0e7dac, relative file paths were joined to the live terminal cwd, TERMINAL_CWD, or process cwd without first guaranteeing that the selected base was absolute. The write and replace-patch entry points separately resolved paths for locking and staleness checks but passed the caller's original path to the lower file-operations layer. Consequently, tool-layer checks and the actual edit could resolve the same relative path from different working directories, allowing an edit intended for a worktree to land in another checkout without the successful response naming the actual target.
episode.after: At pinned ref 96643b4a52b118477b07c838e30eb8ae7372062c, relative paths use a single absolute base selected in precedence order from the task's live terminal cwd, TERMINAL_CWD, and process cwd; relative configured bases are anchored once to the process cwd. Write and replace-patch operations pass the resulting absolute target to the lower layer, successful responses expose resolved_path and files_modified, and relative targets outside an available live workspace produce a warning. Eleven focused tests cover base precedence, absolute-path preservation, divergence-warning conditions, successful write routing, successful replace-patch routing, and protection of a decoy checkout.
episode.diff: The commit adds _resolve_base_dir, rewrites _resolve_path_for_task around its absolute-base invariant, adds _path_resolution_warning, changes write_file_tool and replace-mode patch_tool to operate on pre-resolved absolute targets, enriches successful mutation responses with absolute target metadata, and adds tests/tools/test_file_tools_cwd_resolution.py. The implementation file changes by 103 insertions and 10 deletions, with 197 lines of new focused tests.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 96643b4a52b118477b07c838e30eb8ae7372062c, its first parent is 0c6e133c0434ec856d4aea2b08f216f36c0e7dac, and it changes tools/file_tools.py plus a new focused test file.
The parent implementation selected a live/config/process base, joined it directly to a relative input, and called Path.resolve without an explicit invariant that the base itself was absolute.

The new base resolver gives the live task terminal cwd precedence over TERMINAL_CWD and the process cwd, anchors any relative base to os.getcwd(), resolves it, and therefore always returns an absolute base.
write_file_tool now passes its pre-resolved absolute target to file_ops.write_file instead of the original caller path; successful output includes resolved_path and a one-element files_modified list.

Replace-mode patching now passes the corresponding pre-resolved target to file_ops.patch_replace; successful patch output reports resolved modified paths and reports resolved_path for a single target.
The divergence checker returns no warning for absolute inputs, missing live cwd, or targets inside the live workspace, but names both locations when a relative input resolves outside that workspace.
The write and patch call sites add the divergence warning after higher-priority cross-agent and per-task staleness warnings, so existing warnings retain precedence.
evidence_units.source: git show 96643b4a52b118477b07c838e30eb8ae7372062c:tools/file_tools.py, write_file_tool and patch_tool warning selection

evidence_units.claim: At the pinned ref, the shared path resolver is also used by file-operation lookup, sensitive-path and profile checks, reads, timestamp tracking, and staleness checks, making the absolute-base contract common to those consumers.

Five tests establish base behavior: relative TERMINAL_CWD is anchored absolutely, live tracking wins, an absolute configured cwd is honored, absolute input is not re-anchored, and absent configuration falls back to an absolute process cwd.
Four tests establish the warning boundary: warn for a relative target outside the live workspace, but not for an inside target, an absolute input, or absence of a live cwd.
The write regression test asserts that a relative write modifies the live workspace, returns its absolute resolved_path, and returns the same path in files_modified.

The replace-patch regression test asserts that a relative patch modifies the live workspace, reports its absolute target, and leaves the identically named file in a decoy process-cwd checkout untouched.

The commit message reports 11 new unit tests, 43 live end-to-end assertions, and 466 existing file/path/terminal tests passing; only the committed focused-test source was directly inspectable in this environment.

candidate_workflows.title: Keep relative file mutations anchored to the active workspace
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for repairing file tools whose coordination checks and actual mutations can interpret relative paths from different roots, especially across a main checkout and a worktree.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a relative file mutation is resolved, executed, coordinated, and reported against one absolute target associated with the task's active workspace, while making detectable divergence visible.
when_to_use: A tool resolves or checks a relative file path before delegating the actual mutation to another component that may have a different working directory.
A process can operate in one checkout while a task terminal or worktree operates in another.
Successful mutation responses do not currently reveal the absolute on-disk target, making wrong-root edits difficult to diagnose.
anti_goals: Do not infer that every relative configured cwd identifies the intended workspace; canonicalization makes it deterministic, while live task cwd supplies workspace authority when available.
Do not re-anchor caller-supplied absolute paths under the active workspace.
Do not turn the workspace-divergence diagnostic into a blanket prohibition against intentional outside-workspace absolute paths.
Do not replace or lower the priority of existing concurrency and staleness diagnostics.
Do not broaden this workflow into redesigning file contents, patch matching, or general filesystem authorization.
not_applicable_when: All mutation APIs require absolute paths and no layer independently reinterprets them.
The system has no task-specific or configured root concept and deliberately defines relative paths solely against one immutable process cwd.
The observed failure is caused by patch-content mismatch, permissions, or filesystem errors rather than disagreement about the path root.

title: Preserve literal file paths containing glob metacharacters across workspace-rooted file tools
before: At parent commit fb3ceb0da4e2cd636013c2c36a9c0016c01aa47f, both file-discovery operations passed user inputs directly to the glob library after only separator normalization in the multi-file reader. Consequently, an existing workspace-relative path containing glob metacharacters such as square brackets was interpreted as a pattern rather than as the literal path, so exact files such as file[1].txt or src/app/[test]/(dashboard)/testing/components/code.tsx could be missed.
after: At commit 6fc68ff8d4536f35f0ed76af535d5e1e7ac37675, each operation resolves an input against every applicable workspace search directory, checks whether that exact path exists, and escapes the input before glob evaluation when it does. Nonexistent inputs remain unescaped and therefore retain wildcard-pattern behavior. Focused tests cover literal bracketed filenames and nested paths containing square brackets and parentheses for both discovery and multi-file reading.
diff: The change imports filesystem existence checks and the glob library's escape helper. The discovery operation now classifies its single input independently for each search directory and escapes an existing literal path. The multi-file reader similarly normalizes and classifies every search input independently for each workspace root, passing escaped existing paths and unchanged nonexisting patterns to glob. Four regression tests were added: two for discovery and two for reading. Existing workspace selection, ignore filtering, containment checks, result formatting, and wildcard behavior were left in place.

episode.title: Preserve literal file paths containing glob metacharacters across workspace-rooted file tools
episode.before: At parent commit fb3ceb0da4e2cd636013c2c36a9c0016c01aa47f, both file-discovery operations passed user inputs directly to the glob library after only separator normalization in the multi-file reader. Consequently, an existing workspace-relative path containing glob metacharacters such as square brackets was interpreted as a pattern rather than as the literal path, so exact files such as file[1].txt or src/app/[test]/(dashboard)/testing/components/code.tsx could be missed.
episode.after: At commit 6fc68ff8d4536f35f0ed76af535d5e1e7ac37675, each operation resolves an input against every applicable workspace search directory, checks whether that exact path exists, and escapes the input before glob evaluation when it does. Nonexistent inputs remain unescaped and therefore retain wildcard-pattern behavior. Focused tests cover literal bracketed filenames and nested paths containing square brackets and parentheses for both discovery and multi-file reading.
episode.diff: The change imports filesystem existence checks and the glob library's escape helper. The discovery operation now classifies its single input independently for each search directory and escapes an existing literal path. The multi-file reader similarly normalizes and classifies every search input independently for each workspace root, passing escaped existing paths and unchanged nonexisting patterns to glob. Four regression tests were added: two for discovery and two for reading. Existing workspace selection, ignore filtering, containment checks, result formatting, and wildcard behavior were left in place.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 6fc68ff8d4536f35f0ed76af535d5e1e7ac37675 has parent fb3ceb0da4e2cd636013c2c36a9c0016c01aa47f, is titled "fix(tools): Handle special characters in file paths for glob and read_many_files (#6507)", and changes two implementations plus their two test files.

Before the change, the discovery operation called glob(this.params.pattern, { cwd: searchDir, ... }) directly for every workspace search directory, with no exact-path existence check or escaping step.

After the change, the discovery operation joins each search directory with the supplied input, checks fs.existsSync(fullPath), escapes the input when the exact path exists, and then evaluates the resulting value with cwd set to that search directory.

Before the change, the multi-file reader normalized backslashes in all search inputs and passed the resulting array directly to glob for each workspace directory; it did not distinguish existing literal paths from patterns.

After the change, the multi-file reader processes every input separately under every workspace directory: it normalizes separators, joins the input to the current directory, escapes it if that exact path exists, otherwise preserves it as a glob pattern, and then evaluates the processed array.

The implementation diff adds fs/existsSync and glob escape usage, replacing direct glob submission with existence-gated escaping while retaining the surrounding workspace iteration and filtering pipeline.

Discovery regression tests create file[1].txt and a nested src/app/[test]/(dashboard)/testing/components/code.tsx file, invoke the tool with each exact relative path, and require one result containing the literal created path.

Multi-file-reader regression tests create the same two forms of special-character paths, request each exact relative path, and require the returned content and success display to identify exactly one file.

The discovery test suite retains tests using wildcard inputs such as *.TXT, sub/*.md, and **/*.log, establishing that wildcard interpretation remains part of the required contract alongside the new literal-path behavior.
The changed discovery and multi-file reader classes are registered as core tools, and the core prompt directs the agent to use them for repository discovery and contextual reading.

title: Turn heterogeneous file-edit tool output into compact, reviewable chat diffs
before: At first parent b9f302441fb3fc7927507ccd074a806d600b34d3, the desktop chat handled only write_file and edit_file as diff-producing tools, extracted only result.inline_diff, and rendered unified diffs as raw line-oriented blocks retaining file headers, hunk markers, and +/- markers. Patch results using result.diff were therefore not normalized into the same review surface, and file-edit rows could expose generic action labels or raw argument/result detail instead of a filename-centered review summary.
after: At pinned merge commit 04a1d9efd76db1c5860bd5b928da95e37babb8b7, write_file, edit_file, and patch share one file-edit classification; diffs are accepted from inline_diff or diff; the view model derives basename/full-path metadata, suppresses redundant raw detail, and counts additions/removals. The disclosure row defaults open when a diff exists, shows a file-type icon, filename, path tooltip, and +N/-N statistics, and renders a bounded FileDiffPanel. The panel removes leading file metadata and hunk markers, strips diff markers while preserving change kind, applies add/remove accents, syntax-highlights recognized and budget-safe file types, and falls back to a plain colored renderer. Completed successful edit rows lacking a reviewable diff are hidden, while pending and failed edits remain visible.
diff: Relative to first parent b9f302441fb3fc7927507ccd074a806d600b34d3, the pinned merge changes eight desktop files with 634 insertions and 80 deletions. The behavioral implementation centralizes file-edit recognition and result normalization in the tool view model, replaces the raw diff presentation with a parsed review panel, adds filename-to-icon/language resolution, integrates review metadata and disclosure behavior into the tool row, shares the Shiki theme with code blocks, and adjusts row/diff styling. Focused model tests were added for both accepted diff fields, patch-detail suppression, pending-path presentation, and exclusion of diff headers from line statistics.

episode.title: Turn heterogeneous file-edit tool output into compact, reviewable chat diffs
episode.before: At first parent b9f302441fb3fc7927507ccd074a806d600b34d3, the desktop chat handled only write_file and edit_file as diff-producing tools, extracted only result.inline_diff, and rendered unified diffs as raw line-oriented blocks retaining file headers, hunk markers, and +/- markers. Patch results using result.diff were therefore not normalized into the same review surface, and file-edit rows could expose generic action labels or raw argument/result detail instead of a filename-centered review summary.
episode.after: At pinned merge commit 04a1d9efd76db1c5860bd5b928da95e37babb8b7, write_file, edit_file, and patch share one file-edit classification; diffs are accepted from inline_diff or diff; the view model derives basename/full-path metadata, suppresses redundant raw detail, and counts additions/removals. The disclosure row defaults open when a diff exists, shows a file-type icon, filename, path tooltip, and +N/-N statistics, and renders a bounded FileDiffPanel. The panel removes leading file metadata and hunk markers, strips diff markers while preserving change kind, applies add/remove accents, syntax-highlights recognized and budget-safe file types, and falls back to a plain colored renderer. Completed successful edit rows lacking a reviewable diff are hidden, while pending and failed edits remain visible.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent b9f302441fb3fc7927507ccd074a806d600b34d3, the pinned merge changes eight desktop files with 634 insertions and 80 deletions. The behavioral implementation centralizes file-edit recognition and result normalization in the tool view model, replaces the raw diff presentation with a parsed review panel, adds filename-to-icon/language resolution, integrates review metadata and disclosure behavior into the tool row, shares the Shiki theme with code blocks, and adjusts row/diff styling. Focused model tests were added for both accepted diff fields, patch-detail suppression, pending-path presentation, and exclusion of diff headers from line statistics.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge commit is 04a1d9efd76db1c5860bd5b928da95e37babb8b7 with first parent b9f302441fb3fc7927507ccd074a806d600b34d3 and subject "feat(desktop): PR-style file diffs in chat (#50731)".

Against its first parent, the pinned commit modifies eight desktop files with 634 insertions and 80 deletions, including the tool view model, tool fallback component, diff renderer, filename-language mapping, tests, and styles.

The after-state defines one file-edit classification containing edit_file, patch, and write_file, counts +/- lines while excluding +++/--- headers, and derives edit paths from arguments, result fields, or diff metadata.

The parent recognized only write_file and edit_file in relevant branches and inlineDiffFromResult read only inline_diff; the after-state routes patch through the same classification and accepts both inline_diff and diff.

For normalized file edits, the view model uses the basename as the dynamic title, preserves the path as subtitle, suppresses ordinary detail when a diff or path already conveys the result, and copies the diff preferentially.

The diff renderer removes leading Git/Hermes file-header metadata, drops hunk markers with separators between hunks, strips the leading diff marker, and retains add/context/remove kinds for line-level styling.

FileDiffPanel selects syntax highlighting from the file path only when a known language exists and the diff is within the highlight budget; otherwise it uses the plain change-colored renderer, while the asynchronous highlighting path also displays the plain renderer until ready.
Filename extension mapping supplies both shared file-type icons and bundled Shiki language identifiers, returning an empty language for unknown extensions so callers can fall back safely.

The chat tool row obtains live or persisted diffs, defaults the disclosure open when a diff exists, computes line statistics, shows filename/path-oriented metadata, and passes the normalized diff and path to FileDiffPanel.

A completed successful file-edit row with no diff is omitted as non-reviewable, but pending and error rows are retained; technical raw payload remains available behind a details disclosure when a diff is present.

Focused tests prove that both inline_diff and diff are accepted, a patch diff produces basename title plus full-path subtitle without raw patch detail, and a pending patch shows its path rather than argument JSON.
A focused test proves addition/removal statistics count actual changed lines while excluding unified-diff file headers.

The constituent implementation commits describe the intended behavior as a PR-style per-edit review, followed by filename-aware syntax highlighting with an unknown-language/over-budget/loading fallback and a shared lower-contrast dark theme.
The local evidence bundle identifies repository NousResearch/hermes-agent and issue/PR 50731 but reports the issue body, comments, timeline, PR body, reviews, and status checks as unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: normalize-file-edit-review-data
candidate_atomics.title: Normalize file-edit results into one review model
candidate_atomics.description: Classify all supported mutation tools under one semantic role, reconcile live and persisted diff fields, derive stable file identity, suppress redundant payload detail, and calculate review statistics without counting diff metadata.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure every supported file mutation that carries a unified diff reaches the same review surface with concise identity and accurate change counts.
semantic_action.module_role: file-edit result adaptation and review-view modeling
semantic_action.pre_state: Mutation events may use different tool names and may place their unified diff in either a live side channel, inline_diff, or diff; generic formatting may expose raw arguments or fail to recognize the event as reviewable.
semantic_action.post_state: Recognized file mutations expose one normalized diff, basename title, full-path subtitle when available, empty redundant detail, and addition/removal counts that exclude file-header lines.
semantic_action.validation: Run the focused view-model tests asserting both diff-field variants, patch title/subtitle/detail behavior, pending-path behavior, and header-excluding line counts.

candidate_atomics.name: transform-unified-diff-for-review
candidate_atomics.title: Transform a unified diff into a readable review panel
candidate_atomics.description: Parse unified-diff structure into semantic line kinds, remove transport-oriented chrome, preserve code indentation, layer change accents over optional filename-derived syntax highlighting, and retain a bounded plain-renderer fallback.

semantic_action.intent: Make an edit diff readable as code review content rather than as raw patch protocol text, without making rendering depend on successful syntax highlighting.
semantic_action.pre_state: The available diff contains file headers, hunk coordinates, and +/- gutter markers and may have an unknown language, exceed the syntax-highlighting budget, or still be waiting for the highlighter.
semantic_action.post_state: Renderable lines omit leading file metadata and hunk coordinates, retain add/remove/context semantics and indentation, use bounded scrolling and change accents, and show syntax colors only when safely available while otherwise remaining readable in plain form.
semantic_action.validation: Render representative unified diffs and verify that header and hunk text are absent, changed lines retain their correct kind after marker removal, known budget-safe file paths use the syntax path, and unknown, over-budget, and loading states use the plain renderer.

candidate_atomics.name: integrate-diff-review-disclosure
candidate_atomics.title: Integrate diff review into navigable tool disclosures
candidate_atomics.description: Present each reviewable edit as an automatically expanded disclosure with file identity, change statistics, copy access, and raw technical drill-down, while omitting only settled successful rows that lack review content.

semantic_action.intent: Let a reviewer identify, open, scan, copy, and optionally inspect the raw payload of each file edit directly in the conversation without clutter from non-reviewable duplicates.
semantic_action.module_role: conversation review navigation and disclosure lifecycle
semantic_action.pre_state: File mutations appear as generic tool rows whose review content and identity are not consistently surfaced; rehydrated successful edits may leave empty duplicate rows.
semantic_action.post_state: A diff-bearing edit defaults open and exposes filename, path tooltip, file icon, +N/-N summary, bounded review panel, copy action, and optional technical payload; only completed successful edit rows with no diff are hidden, while pending and failed rows remain visible.
semantic_action.validation: Use the tested line-count helper for header statistics, then exercise the disclosure component with diff-bearing, pending, failed, and settled diff-less edit fixtures to verify open state, metadata, panel wiring, technical drill-down, and visibility rules.

candidate_workflows.name: convert-file-edit-events-into-reviewable-chat-diffs
candidate_workflows.title: Convert heterogeneous file-edit events into navigable code-review panels
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order implementation workflow for adapting multiple mutation event shapes into a consistent, resilient diff-review experience embedded in a conversational tool stream.

workflow_graph.goal: Every supported file mutation carrying a unified diff is presented as a concise, navigable, and readable per-file review without exposing redundant raw payloads or depending on syntax-highlighter availability.
when_to_use: A conversational or activity-stream interface receives file mutations from multiple tool/event shapes and reviewers need to inspect the resulting code changes in place.
Mutation results already provide, or can be reconciled to, unified-diff text and a stable event identity.
Raw patch output currently includes transport metadata or generic tool payload detail that obscures the changed code.
anti_goals: Do not alter the semantics or contents of the underlying file mutation.
Do not count unified-diff file headers as additions or removals.
Do not require syntax highlighting for a diff to remain visible and readable.
Do not hide pending mutations or failed mutations merely because they lack a diff.
Do not remove access to raw diagnostic payloads when a technical drill-down mode is required.
not_applicable_when: The event has no file mutation semantics and no unified-diff representation.
The product requires an exact raw patch display including file headers, hunk coordinates, and +/- markers as its primary view.
The interface has no per-event disclosure or equivalent navigation surface in which review content can be presented.
inputs: Supported mutation-tool or event identifiers
Tool arguments and persisted result payloads
Optional live diff keyed by event/tool-call identity
Unified-diff text
File path or filename metadata
Disclosure and technical-view state
Syntax-language mapping and rendering budget
workflow_graph.entry_state: File-edit events are rendered through generic tool-result formatting; supported names and diff fields are inconsistent, and raw unified-diff protocol text or argument JSON is exposed to the reviewer.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All admitted file-edit events with diffs use one normalized review contract and appear as filename-centered disclosures with accurate statistics and a resilient parsed diff panel; settled successful rows without review content are omitted without suppressing pending or error state.

steps.condition: Apply when a tool/event represents a file mutation and may expose a diff through live state, inline_diff, or diff.
steps.validation: Focused model tests accept both persisted fields, preserve the patch path during pending and completed states, suppress redundant detail, and return accurate +N/-N counts.

steps.condition: Apply when normalization yields non-empty unified-diff text.

commit.subject: Limit inline diff previews in the TUI (#41143)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

Large or minified diffs can require substantial work to allocate wrapped rows and syntax-highlighted spans in the inline patch view.

## What changed

- Limit inline patch previews to 12 rendered rows across all changed files, while retaining file summaries and directing users to the transcript when content is omitted.
- Preserve complete diff content in transcript and raw views.
- Bound preview source scanning to 64 KiB so zero-width content cannot bypass the row budget.

## Testing

Add coverage for added, deleted, updated, renamed, minified, narrow-width, wide-character, combining-character, and multi-file diffs, including preservation of complete transcript and raw output.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1899129ab548771c29d226ff624549573fb2f688

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, PatchHistoryCell::display_lines called create_diff_summary, and raw_lines called the same renderer at RAW_DIFF_SUMMARY_WIDTH; no dedicated transcript override or bounded preview renderer existed.
The renderer gained create_diff_preview, which calls the shared block renderer with PREVIEW_ROWS, while create_diff_summary calls it with usize::MAX to retain unbounded behavior.

The preview helper defines a 12-row preview and a 64-KiB source ceiling; visible_byte_count accounts for UTF-8 boundaries, character display width, tabs, wrapping, and zero-width content before expensive styling and allocation.

The shared renderer decrements one rendered-row budget across files, uses Paragraph wrapping to measure final row use, preserves per-file headers, stops content rendering after omission, and appends a notice directing the user to the transcript.

Add, delete, and update rendering now restricts highlighting and line construction to a visible source prefix and reports whether content was omitted; callers that pass usize::MAX retain full rendering.
PatchHistoryCell routes display_lines to create_diff_preview and transcript_lines to create_diff_summary, while raw_lines continues to derive plain lines from the full summary.
The minified-diff test asserts a 12-row inline prefix plus an omission/transcript hint and separately asserts that transcript and raw views equal the complete diff summary.

A multi-file test verifies that the content budget is shared across files while all file summaries remain present and an omission notice is shown.
Width-sensitive tests verify exactly 12 rendered body rows at widths 8, 16, 40, and 80 for long ASCII, wide, tabbed, and combining-character inputs.
Small diffs and diffs exactly at the row budget remain identical to the complete summary, including empty and rename-only entries.
Zero-width combining-mark tests verify that scanning stops at the 64-KiB boundary, later file summaries remain visible, and transcript output remains complete for add, delete, and update forms.

candidate_workflows.description: Establish a resource-bounded preview contract, implement display-aware early truncation and omission signaling, then route only the compact surface through it while validating both limits and full-content preservation.

workflow_graph.goal: Keep inline diff presentation responsive and predictably sized while preserving file-level context and complete diff access through dedicated review surfaces.
when_to_use: An inline or feed-style diff surface eagerly wraps, highlights, or allocates rows for complete change content.
Large, minified, narrow-width, wide-character, or zero-width-heavy changes can make preview cost or height effectively unbounded.
A separate transcript, raw, expanded, or detail surface can remain the source of complete content.
anti_goals: Do not impose the preview limit on transcript, raw, expanded, export, or other complete-review surfaces.
Do not remove file summaries or rename metadata merely because the content budget is exhausted.
Do not treat logical source lines alone as the visible budget when viewport wrapping can produce multiple rendered rows.
Do not rely only on display width to bound source scanning, because zero-width input can consume bytes without consuming columns.
Do not truncate small or exact-budget diffs.
not_applicable_when: The surface is itself the canonical complete diff view and no alternate full-content review path exists.
Rendering already performs bounded lazy or virtualized work with an equivalent visible-row and source-scan invariant.
The input is only a file summary and does not render change content.
inputs: A change-set representation covering additions, deletions, updates, and renames
The inline viewport width and wrapping behavior
A rendered-content row budget
A source-scan byte ceiling
The complete-view entry points for transcript, raw, expanded, or equivalent output
A user-visible omission message that identifies the complete review path
workflow_graph.entry_state: One unbounded rendering path supplies inline and complete-review surfaces, so expensive processing and any prospective truncation are not isolated by presentation role.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Inline rendering has bounded row allocation and bounded source scanning across the whole change set, retains summary/navigation context, and signals omissions; complete-review surfaces still expose the full diff.

validation_ladder: Confirm small and exact-budget diffs render identically to the full summary.
Confirm additions, deletions, updates, renames, and multiple files obey one shared rendered-row budget.
Confirm actual wrapped viewport rows remain bounded at narrow and normal widths for ASCII, tabs, wide characters, and combining sequences.
Confirm zero-width-heavy source scanning stops at the byte ceiling without hiding later file summaries.
Confirm an omission notice directs users to the complete review path.
Confirm transcript and raw outputs preserve the complete diff whenever the inline preview is truncated.
stop_conditions: Stop if no distinct complete-review surface can preserve omitted content and product requirements require the inline surface to be complete.
Stop if viewport wrapping or character-width behavior cannot be measured consistently enough to define a rendered-row oracle.
Stop and defer if truncation can hide mandatory metadata rather than content-only rows.
Stop if tests cannot distinguish bounded inline output from complete transcript/raw output.

Parameterized tests verify bounded previews for add, delete, update, and rename cases and verify that transcript output remains complete.
A multi-file test verifies that the content budget is shared across files while all file summaries remain present and an omission notice is shown.
Width-sensitive tests verify exactly 12 rendered body rows at widths 8, 16, 40, and 80 for long ASCII, wide, tabbed, and combining-character inputs.
Small diffs and diffs exactly at the row budget remain identical to the complete summary, including empty and rename-only entries.
Zero-width combining-mark tests verify that scanning stops at the 64-KiB boundary, later file summaries remain visible, and transcript output remains complete for add, delete, and update forms.

title: Add bounded, workspace-scoped working-tree diff review
before: At parent a0ce04a9929527a7884422842a8079e0af99ead0, the core could compute aggregate working-tree statistics and whole-tree hunks, but it had no on-demand single-file hunk operation. The daemon had no working-tree diff REST routes or SDK methods, and the web shell had no Changes dialog, workspace-scoped diff state, or local /diff navigation.
after: Commit 582fb49603c74158e13f735cdfa97e987d0c58d2 adds a read-only review path from core through daemon routes and SDK to the web shell. It lists changed files with bounded statistics, lazily fetches normalized single-file hunks, synthesizes bounded hunks for regular untracked text files, preserves rename and no-newline semantics, exposes truncation, rejects unsafe paths and untrusted workspaces, and renders expandable per-file changes with independent old/new-side highlighting, loading/error states, and workspace-correct navigation from /diff, the active status chip, or a sidebar workspace.
diff: The implementation adds workspace Git-diff list and single-file routes, registers their bound and workspace-qualified variants, adds optional additive SDK wire types and client methods, extends core diff parsing and retrieval for per-file lazy loading, and introduces a Changes dialog plus entry-point state in the web shell. Supporting tests cover route serialization and trust gates, SDK URL encoding, rename-aware retrieval, traversal rejection, tracked and untracked truncation, FIFO avoidance, lazy expansion, syntax highlighting, failure degradation, hidden-file notices, and /diff interception.

All git access goes through the daemon REST API with per-workspace trust
gating; new SDK status fields are optional and additive (v2).

* fix(web-shell): themed tooltips and git-chip review follow-ups

Tooltips now render on the themed popover surface (bg-popover /
text-popover-foreground / border + fill-popover arrow) instead of the
inverted bg-foreground default, so they read dark-o

feat(web-shell): git status chip, visual working-tree diff, and sidebar git status (#7054)

* feat(web-shell): git status chip, visual working-tree diff, and sidebar git status

Bring working-tree Git awareness to the Web Shell (browser daemon session UI):

- Toolbar branch chip becomes a live status indicator: dirty (staged/unstaged/
  untracked), ahead/behind upstream, stash count, detached HEAD, in-progress
  operation (merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert/bisect), and conflict count, each
  with a non-color cue.
- Read-only "Changes" dialog: working-tree-vs-HEAD file list with per-file,
  line-level, per-side syntax-highlighted diffs; opens via /diff or a dirty
  chip; untracked files expand as fully-added and deleted files still diff.
- Per-workspace git status in the sidebar: a compact icon-only chip per trusted
  workspace (status dot + hover tooltip); click opens that workspace's dialog.

All git access goes through the daemon REST API with per-workspace trust
gating; new SDK status fields are optional and additive (v2).

* fix(web-shell): themed tooltips and git-chip review follow-ups

Tooltips now render on the themed popover surface (bg-popover /
text-popover-foreground / border + fill-popover arrow) instead of the
inverted bg-foreground default, so they read dark-on-dark rather than a
bright box on the dark theme. Fixing the shared primitive corrects the
git branch tooltip in the composer toolbar and sidebar, plus every other
tooltip, at once.

Also addressing review feedback on the git integration:
- Replace the hand-drawn detached/conflict/stash SVG icons with
  lucide-react (CircleDot / TriangleAlert / Layers) per the web-shell
  icon convention.
- Gate the tooltip "Working tree clean" message on an enriched status
  (computedAt) so a branch-only status no longer asserts clean.
- Include the file path in the diff dialog row aria-label so screen
  readers can distinguish files.
- Reset the toolbar git chip on workspace switch so it never shows the
  previous repo's branch/counts while the new fetch resolves.
- Log a sidebar git poll failure only on the success->failure transition
  to avoid spamming a long-lived tab.
- Correct the SDK doc for DaemonWorkspaceGitDiffFile.added/removed
  (0, not undefined, for binary files).

* fix(web-shell): address git-integration review suggestions

Follow-ups from the /review pass on the git integration:

- GitBranchIndicator: include the short SHA in the detached-HEAD tooltip
  title, and add the "Working tree clean" status to the aria-label (gated
  on an enriched status, matching the tooltip) so the two never drift.
- WorkspaceSection: keep the last known git status on a transient poll
  failure instead of blanking the chip for a whole interval.
- App: surface a toast for `/diff` when no workspace is available instead
  of silently consuming the composer input.
- Tests: cover the diff dialog's list-load and per-file load error paths,
  and detectGitOperation's revert/bisect branches.
- Design doc: align the getGitWorkingTreeStatus spec text with the
  decision (transient states return status with `operation`; null is
  reserved for non-repo / git failure).

* fix(web-shell): focus-visible ring for git chip button; align doc poll interval

- Add a :focus-visible outline to .gitBranchChipButton so keyboard users
  get a visible focus indicator (the chip resets UA button chrome).
- Design doc: align the active-workspace poll-interval references at 30s
  to match the implementation.

* fix(web-shell): surface capped diffs, catch row-build failures, cover degradation paths

Address the remaining review findings on the git integration:

- Truncation is no longer silent: fetchGitDiffHunksForFile now returns
  { hunks, truncated } — the parser records files that actually lost
  lines to MAX_LINES_PER_FILE (tracked path), and the untracked
  synthesis reports its byte/line caps. The route forwards an additive
  `truncated` flag on the hunks response (absent when not truncated, so
  older clients and daemons are unaffected), and the Changes dialog
  renders a "Diff truncated" note under the visible window.
- DiffHunks catches an unexpected buildRows rejection (e.g. malformed
  hunk lines) and shows the per-file error instead of leaving an
  unhandled rejection and a silently empty diff area.
- New tests: untracked and tracked truncation at the core caps, the
  route's truncated passthrough (and its absence when clean), the
  branch-only degradation when the working-tree summary throws, the
  malformed-hunks error path, and the Shiki success path (a fake
  tokenizer proving add rows pull new-side tokens and del rows pull
  old-side tokens, not the plain-text fallback).

* fix(web-shell): drop dialog backdrop-blur that froze the page on open

The dialog and alert-dialog overlays applied `backdrop-blur-xs`, which
forces the browser to rasterize and blur the entire content behind the
overlay when a dialog opens. With a long transcript behind it, that
main-thread paint+blur froze the whole page — e.g. clicking the git
branch chip to open the Changes dialog. Keep the bg-black/10 scrim for
separation and drop the blur.

* fix(core): guard synthesizeUntrackedHunk against non-regular files

synthesizeUntrackedHunk opened an untracked path before checking its
type, so an untracked FIFO (listed by `ls-files --others`) would block
on open() forever waiting on a writer — hanging the daemon's event loop
and leaving the Web Shell Changes dialog stuck on a permanent loading
state. lstat-gate on regular files before opening, matching the existing
guard in countUntrackedLines. Adds a FIFO regression test.

* fix(web-shell,core): rename expansion, no-newline marker, chip measurement

Round-5 review Criticals:

- core: key renamed diff entries by the real (post-rename) path and carry
  the old path for display, so renamed rows can be expanded — the synthetic
  `old => new` key was sent to git as a nonexistent literal path. The diff
  dialog renders the rename as `old → new`.
- core: preserve Git's `\ No newline at end of file` marker through the hunk
  parser so a trailing-newline-only edit isn't shown as identical
  removed/added lines (the viewer already renders it as a meta row).
- web-shell: the toolbar's hidden git-chip measurement replica now renders
  the full chip content via the extracted GitBranchChipContent, so the
  expanded width includes the status indicators and the compact/expanded
  toggle no longer oscillates near the responsive threshold.

* fix(build): generate git-commit info even when prepare build is skipped

The review tooling runs `npm ci` with QWEN_SKIP_PREPARE=1 (to skip the
heavy prepare build) and then builds only the changed workspaces. Because
`prepare` exited before generating the gitignored git-commit.ts, a
per-workspace build of packages/cli failed at the unchanged systemInfo.ts
on the missing `../generated/git-commit.js` module. Generate the git-commit
info in the skip path too — it is cheap and never fails hard — so a later
per-workspace build or typecheck finds the module. The non-skip path still
generates it via `npm run build`.

* fix(web-shell,cli): address round-6 review suggestions

- cli: carry the pre-rename path (oldPath) through DiffRenderRow and show
  renamed files as `old → new` in both the Ink and plain-text renderers.
  The rename-keying fix updated the daemon and web-shell dialog but not the
  CLI `/diff` renderer, which silently dropped the old path.
- web-shell: key DiffFileRow by workspace + path so switching workspace
  remounts the row instead of reusing another workspace's hunks/open state
  for a path both workspaces share.
- web-shell: show a loading placeholder in DiffHunks while rows are (re)built
  (e.g. after a theme switch) instead of an empty, jumpily-resized box.
- web-shell: cover the /diff local intercept in App.test.tsx (opens the
  Changes dialog and is not forwarded to the agent).

* fix(web-shell,cli,core): address round-7 review suggestions

- cli: sanitize the rendered filename (and pre-rename oldPath) in the Ink
  DiffStatsDisplay via sanitizeFilenameForDisplay, matching the plain-text
  renderer so a crafted path can't inject into the interactive view.
- cli: apply the read headers before awaiting the per-file diff fetch (as
  handleDiffList does) so error responses also carry no-store/nosniff.
- cli + web-shell: strip Unicode bidi embedding/isolate controls
  (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069) in the filename/control-char sanitizers so a
  crafted filename can't visually spoof its extension.
- core: guard countStashEntries with an lstat type check before readFile, so
  a symlink-to-FIFO at logs/refs/stash can't block the event loop (the same
  hazard already guarded in the untracked-file readers).
- core: cover fetchGitDiffHunksForFile's transient-state guard with a test
  (the sibling helpers already had one).

* fix(web-shell,cli,core): address round-8 review suggestions

- core: pass --no-optional-locks to the ls-files call in
  fetchGitDiffHunksForFile, matching the other runGit calls so it doesn't
  contend for an optional index-refresh lock alongside concurrent git
  add/commit.
- cli: add a route test asserting a rename's oldPath survives serialization
  end-to-end (keyed by the new path, old path carried alongside).
- web-shell: add a GitDiffDialog test for the hiddenCount>0 "N more files
  not shown" note (every payload previously used hiddenCount: 0).
- web-shell: drop the nonexistent primaryLabel prop from the WorkspaceSection
  test (it is not a WorkspaceSectionProps member).
- docs: correct the plan doc — large-diff virtual scrolling was explicitly
  descoped (core caps + per-file lazy loading), not implemented in Phase 2.

* fix(cli,web-shell): address round-9 review findings

- cli: propagate the pre-rename oldPath through DiffDialog's
  perFileToUnified and render renamed files as `old → new` in the
  interactive diff viewer (the rename-keying fix had updated the daemon,
  the web-shell dialog, and the /diff stats, but not this viewer).
- cli: cover DiffStatsDisplay's rename (`old → new`) rendering and the
  sanitizeFilenameForDisplay path for hostile filenames carrying control
  characters.
- web-shell: guard the GitBranchIndicator test afterEach against
  double-unmounting an already-unmounted root (the localization tests
  assert on getTranslator without calling render()).

* fix(core,cli,web-shell): rename-aware single-file diff (old→new)

fetchGitDiffHunksForFile pathspec-limited the diff to the new path, which
defeats git's rename detection — a renamed file was reported as fully
added (every line +) instead of its actual edit. Thread an optional
pre-rename path through the single-file endpoint (core → route → SDK →
dialog) and diff old→new with -M when it is present, so expanding a
renamed file shows its real content change.

* fix(cli): address round-10 review suggestions

- DiffDialog: split the path-width budget between old and new paths for a
  rename (reserving the " → " separator) so the combined width stays within
  maxPathChars instead of overflowing the row layout.
- textUtils: extend MULTILINE_CONTROL_CHARS_REGEX with the Unicode bidi
  ranges (matching FILENAME_CONTROL_CHARS_REGEX) and add a test that
  sanitizeFilenameForDisplay strips bidi embedding/isolate controls.
- workspace-git-diff route: add a test that ?oldPath= is parsed and
  forwarded to fetchGitDiffHunksForFile.

* test(sdk),docs: cover diff client methods; align design doc

- sdk: add DaemonClient unit tests for workspaceGitDiff() and
  workspaceGitDiffFile(path, oldPath?) — URL construction (incl. urlEncode
  on path/oldPath, with and without oldPath, plus the workspace-qualified
  route) and response deserialization, mirroring the existing workspaceGit()
  test.
- docs: add the oldPath? param to the workspaceGitDiffFile API spec; record
  that the diff client methods now have unit tests (correcting the claim
  that workspaceGit() had none); attribute the bundle-limit bump to
  packages/sdk-typescript/scripts/build.js; clarify ahead/behind are relative
  to upstream (0, and ↑N/↓N not shown, without one).

* fix(web-shell,core): address round-11 review suggestions

- GitBranchIndicator: count conflicted entries as dirty — a merge where every
  changed file is conflicted (staged=unstaged=untracked=0) is still
  uncommitted, so the expanded chip's dirty dot / data-dirty now reflect it.
- core: split the status branch line at the last "..." (the branch/upstream
  separator) so a dotted branch name isn't truncated at the first "...".
- GitDiffDialog: guard DiffFileRow's in-flight fetch against unmount via a
  cancelled ref, matching DiffHunks / GitDiffDialog.
- tests: forward oldPath when expanding a renamed file in the web-shell
  dialog; bidi-strip coverage for the web-shell sanitizeControlChars;
  untrusted-guard coverage on the single-file diff route; conflicted-only
  dirty; branch-line "..." split.

* fix(web-shell,cli): address round-12 review suggestions

- DiffDialog: only render the rename "old → new" when there's room for both
  sides (≥19 cols, so each gets ≥8); otherwise fall back to the new path
  alone, so a narrow terminal no longer overflows the row (the Math.max(8,…)
  floor could exceed maxPathChars).
- GitBranchIndicator test: guard afterEach container.remove() for non-render
  tests run in isolation, and make the compact-mode ↑-suppression assertion
  non-vacuous by giving the fixture an ahead count.
- App: compute the active workspace once (useMemo) and share it between the
  git-status effect and the Changes-dialog entry point, so the chip and the
  dialog can't drift onto different repos.

* fix(core,docs): address round-13 review suggestions

- core: add a rebase-apply detection test (git am / an interrupted
  `rebase --apply` creates rebase-apply, which detectGitOperation also maps
  to 'rebase'); previously only rebase-merge was exercised.
- docs: correct section 5 to describe the actual diff-dialog mechanism
  (diffWorkspaceCwd state, not the stale activePanel design).

* test(core): cover stray no-newline marker before any hunk header

parseGitDiff's pre-hunk guard already skips a "\ No newline at end of
file" marker that appears before any @@ header, so a malformed/truncated
diff can't throw on a null currentHunk and lose subsequent files' hunks;
add a regression test pinning that behavior.

* fix(web-shell): unstick per-file diff loading and skip non-path git poll

- DiffFileRow: reset the cancelled-fetch flag on mount so StrictMode's
  mount/unmount/mount replay no longer leaves it latched at true, which
  dropped the fetched hunks and froze the row on "Loading changes…" despite
  a 200 response.
- WorkspaceSection: skip the git status poll when the workspace cwd is not an
  absolute path. A synthetic fallback workspace carries a display name there,
  which the cwd-qualified route rejects with a 400.

* fix(web-shell,cli): address review suggestions on the git diff surface

- GitDiffDialog: highlight each diff side independently so a small side
  keeps syntax highlighting even when the other side exceeds the size cap
  (the old guard dropped both as soon as either was too large).
- ChatEditor: complete the .gitBranchChipButton reset (font/color/padding/
  margin) so the clickable dirty-tree chip matches the read-only output chip
  instead of picking up UA button styling.
- DiffDialog: cover the interactive rename display (old to new on a wide
  terminal), mirroring the rename tests DiffStatsDisplay and GitDiffDialog
  already have.

* test(web-shell,cli): cover git chip clean/reload/traversal paths, fix doc

- GitDiffDialog: add the missing expect(header).not.toBeNull() guard to the
  three expand-file tests that lacked it, matching the others in the block.
- GitBranchIndicator: cover the known-clean aria-label branch (computedAt set
  and every change counter zero).
- WorkspaceSection: verify a reloadToken change re-fetches git status instead
  of waiting for the next 60s poll.
- workspace-git-diff route: verify a traversal oldPath is forwarded to core
  and surfaced as available:false rather than escaping the workspace.
- Design doc: /diff is handled via setDiffWorkspaceCwd, not setActivePanel.

* fix(core): allow literal `..foo` paths in diff normalization

- toRepoRelativePath: reject only a real climb-out (`..` or `../…`), not a
  literal `..foo` filename at the repo root, which the bare startsWith('..')
  over-rejected, leaving the diff viewer unable to render such a file.
- parseGitDiff: cover the truncatedPaths output set directly (it was only
  exercised indirectly through fetchGitDiffHunksForFile).

episode.title: Add bounded, workspace-scoped working-tree diff review
episode.before: At parent a0ce04a9929527a7884422842a8079e0af99ead0, the core could compute aggregate working-tree statistics and whole-tree hunks, but it had no on-demand single-file hunk operation. The daemon had no working-tree diff REST routes or SDK methods, and the web shell had no Changes dialog, workspace-scoped diff state, or local /diff navigation.
episode.after: Commit 582fb49603c74158e13f735cdfa97e987d0c58d2 adds a read-only review path from core through daemon routes and SDK to the web shell. It lists changed files with bounded statistics, lazily fetches normalized single-file hunks, synthesizes bounded hunks for regular untracked text files, preserves rename and no-newline semantics, exposes truncation, rejects unsafe paths and untrusted workspaces, and renders expandable per-file changes with independent old/new-side highlighting, loading/error states, and workspace-correct navigation from /diff, the active status chip, or a sidebar workspace.
episode.diff: The implementation adds workspace Git-diff list and single-file routes, registers their bound and workspace-qualified variants, adds optional additive SDK wire types and client methods, extends core diff parsing and retrieval for per-file lazy loading, and introduces a Changes dialog plus entry-point state in the web shell. Supporting tests cover route serialization and trust gates, SDK URL encoding, rename-aware retrieval, traversal rejection, tracked and untracked truncation, FIFO avoidance, lazy expansion, syntax highlighting, failure degradation, hidden-file notices, and /diff interception.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 582fb49603c74158e13f735cdfa97e987d0c58d2, with parent a0ce04a9929527a7884422842a8079e0af99ead0, and describes a read-only Changes dialog, daemon REST access, workspace trust gating, and optional additive SDK fields.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 582fb49603c74158e13f735cdfa97e987d0c58d2; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0] and commit_show_stat

evidence_units.claim: The parent contains fetchGitDiffHunks for whole-tree retrieval but has neither fetchGitDiffHunksForFile nor the daemon diff route, web-shell GitDiffDialog, or App-level diff navigation state.
evidence_units.source: git show a0ce04a9929527a7884422842a8079e0af99ead0:packages/core/src/utils/gitDiff.ts lines 279-306; git cat-file -e parent:packages/cli/src/serve/routes/workspace-git-diff.ts; git cat-file -e parent:packages/web-shell/client/components/dialogs/GitDiffDialog.tsx; git show parent:packages/web-shell/client/App.tsx

evidence_units.claim: The core adds fetchGitDiffHunksForFile, which normalizes caller paths to repository-relative paths, rejects traversal or outside-root paths, avoids transient Git states, uses rename detection when oldPath is supplied, and disables external diff and text-conversion execution.

Single-file retrieval synthesizes an all-added hunk only for Git-confirmed untracked files, checks that the target is a regular file before opening it, avoids following unsafe file types, detects binary content, and applies byte and line caps while returning an explicit truncated flag.

Diff list and parser contracts retain at most 50 file details, cap individual diff content at 1,000,000 bytes and 400 lines, preserve the post-rename path as the key with oldPath metadata, preserve no-newline markers, and record files whose displayed hunks were truncated.

Core tests verify new-path rename keying, no-newline marker handling, truncation tracking, transient-state rejection, rename-aware old-to-new retrieval, untracked synthesis, tracked and untracked truncation, binary handling, FIFO non-blocking behavior, traversal rejection, and acceptance of a literal ..foo filename.

The daemon exposes list and single-file read routes, applies no-store read headers, serializes oldPath and truncation metadata, validates the required path query, and supports an optional oldPath query for rename-aware retrieval.
Workspace-qualified diff routes resolve the requested runtime and require it to be trusted before invoking either list or single-file retrieval.

Route tests verify list and hunk serialization, oldPath propagation, additive truncated output, missing-path rejection, trusted workspace selection, rejection of untrusted and unknown workspaces, and unavailable output for traversal rejected by the core.
The TypeScript SDK adds workspaceGitDiff and workspaceGitDiffFile methods for bound and workspace-qualified clients and URL-encodes both current and pre-rename paths.
SDK tests verify diff-list deserialization and single-file URL construction with and without oldPath, including the workspace-qualified route.

The web dialog first loads the bounded file list, then fetches hunks only when a non-binary row is expanded; it forwards oldPath, keys rows by workspace and current path, and presents loading, unavailable, empty, binary, error, hidden-file, and truncated states.

Rendered rows maintain old and new line numbers, preserve meta rows, tokenize old and new sides independently, fall back to plain text when highlighting fails, and surface unexpected row-building failures instead of leaving an empty view.

Dialog tests verify file statistics, hidden-count disclosure, lazy expansion, StrictMode loading recovery, rename propagation, unavailable and clean states, binary and untracked labels, list and per-file failures, truncation disclosure, malformed-hunk degradation, and per-side syntax token use.

App state stores the workspace selected for review, intercepts /diff locally instead of forwarding it to the agent, targets the same active workspace used by status polling, renders GitDiffDialog, and passes a workspace-specific open callback to the sidebar.
The App test verifies that submitting /diff opens the Changes dialog and does not forward the command to the agent.

The implementation includes direct unit and route-level oracles across the core parser/retriever, daemon routes, SDK client, dialog component, and App command integration; the evidence bundle identifies the case as implementation_plus_test and a train candidate.

candidate_workflows.name: add_bounded_workspace_diff_review
candidate_workflows.title: Add bounded, workspace-correct change review
candidate_workflows.description: An executable resolution chain for adding a read-only change-review surface that is safe on large or hostile working trees, lazy at file granularity, and correctly scoped across multiple workspaces.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow a user to navigate from a workspace-aware entry point to a read-only changed-file list and expand individual files into bounded, accurate line-level diffs with explicit incomplete and failure states.
when_to_use: A client must review local working-tree changes through a remote, daemon, browser, or otherwise separated presentation layer.
Whole-tree diff retrieval is too expensive or unsafe, so detailed content should be loaded only for the file being reviewed.
The application can address more than one workspace and review actions must retain workspace ownership.
anti_goals: Do not mutate the working tree, index, branch, stash, or repository configuration.
Do not eagerly fetch or syntax-highlight every file in the working tree.
Do not silently present capped content as a complete diff.
Do not bypass workspace trust checks or permit path traversal.
Do not forward a local review-navigation command to an agent or command executor.
not_applicable_when: The product only needs aggregate change counts and no line-level review.
The source cannot provide structured or parseable working-tree changes.
There is no trustworthy workspace or repository boundary against which requested paths can be normalized.
The requested surface is intended to edit, stage, discard, or commit changes rather than remain read-only.
inputs: workspace or repository root
workspace trust and selection metadata
changed-file summary provider
single-file diff provider
current file path and optional pre-rename path
file, byte, and line presentation limits
review entry points and dialog host
workflow_graph.entry_state: The system may expose aggregate change information or whole-tree hunks, but it lacks a complete workspace-scoped path from review navigation to bounded, on-demand per-file presentation.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Each authorized review entry opens the intended workspace's changed-file list; individual rows retrieve safe bounded hunks only when expanded; rename, untracked, deleted, binary, no-newline, hidden-count, truncation, loading, clean, unavailable, and failure states are distinguishable.

steps.condition: Always required when detailed review content is not already available through a safe bounded per-file operation.
steps.validation: Exercise tracked edits, renames, untracked text, binary and special files, transient repository states, traversal attempts, no-newline markers, and both byte and line caps.

steps.condition: Required when the presentation layer does not execute in the same trust and process boundary as the repository reader.
steps.validation: Verify list and hunk serialization, path encoding, old-path propagation, no-store headers, workspace selection, missing queries, trust rejection, and additive truncation metadata.

steps.condition: Required for an interactive visual review surface.
steps.validation: Verify initial list loading, expansion-triggered file retrieval, line mapping, rename display, per-side highlighting, plain-text fallback, remount safety, hidden counts, truncation notes, and explicit error/empty/unavailable states.

steps.condition: Required when review can be opened from commands, active-workspace controls, or workspace-specific navigation.
steps.validation: Verify every entry point passes the intended workspace, local commands are consumed locally, and missing workspace state produces user feedback rather than an unintended request.

validation_ladder: Unit-test normalization and parsing invariants, including rename keys, meta markers, caps, traversal, transient states, untracked files, binary files, and non-regular files.
Route-test trust gating, required parameters, selected workspace propagation, serialization, cache headers, unavailable results, and truncation metadata.
Client-test URL encoding and response deserialization with and without a pre-rename path.
Component-test lazy loading, state transitions, per-side rendering, remount cancellation behavior, error degradation, hidden counts, and truncation disclosure.
Integration-test each navigation entry point to confirm it opens the intended workspace and does not trigger unrelated agent execution.
stop_conditions: Stop if no stable repository root or workspace trust boundary can be established.
Stop if unsafe paths can reach filesystem reads or diff execution outside the repository.
Stop if content limits exist but the client cannot distinguish truncated output from complete output.
Stop if workspace identity is lost between the navigation entry point, API call, and rendered row.
Stop if the only available validation is a title, design document, or commit message without implementation and test oracles.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle does not include CI status checks, PR reviews, or author discussion.
No browser end-to-end performance measurement is included; bounded constants, lazy retrieval, and component tests establish the implemented control strategy but not a measured latency target.
Pattern induction and holdout promotion are deferred because this episode supplies only one repository workflow.

The checkout worktree is not materialized at the pinned commit; evidence was read directly from Git objects at the pinned commit and parent.
No cross-repository Resolution Pattern is emitted because the extraction contract forbids inducing one from a single Issue or Workflow.

title: Preserve the previously focused terminal when closing a programmatically managed diff tab
before: At parent commit 196c772a970166a26fa0e5f92f4fbd89ec265301, the shared diff-closing routine found the matching diff tab and called the editor API as close(tab), without the keep-focus argument. The same routine was used by direct close, accept, and cancel paths, so closing an accepted or rejected diff could move focus from the terminal to an editor.
after: At commit e5b6680332883bd72aaa59292936b184f340256f, the shared routine calls close(tab, true), preserving the focus held outside the diff while retaining existing context reset, tracked-content cleanup, and accept/reject notification behavior. Unit tests assert the keep-focus argument across close, accept, and cancel paths, while an extension-host integration test focuses a terminal, opens and accepts a diff, and verifies that a typing probe does not reach the previously opened editor. The integration test is built, launched through the editor test harness, and added to CI.
diff: The behavioral implementation is a one-argument change in the shared diff-tab cleanup boundary: the matched tab is closed with keepFocus=true. Supporting changes add comprehensive unit coverage and a reusable editor mock, expose a development-only command for opening a diff during extension-host tests, bundle and launch the new integration tests, add the editor test dependency and scripts, and execute the suite in CI under a virtual display on Linux.

episode.title: Preserve the previously focused terminal when closing a programmatically managed diff tab
episode.before: At parent commit 196c772a970166a26fa0e5f92f4fbd89ec265301, the shared diff-closing routine found the matching diff tab and called the editor API as close(tab), without the keep-focus argument. The same routine was used by direct close, accept, and cancel paths, so closing an accepted or rejected diff could move focus from the terminal to an editor.
episode.after: At commit e5b6680332883bd72aaa59292936b184f340256f, the shared routine calls close(tab, true), preserving the focus held outside the diff while retaining existing context reset, tracked-content cleanup, and accept/reject notification behavior. Unit tests assert the keep-focus argument across close, accept, and cancel paths, while an extension-host integration test focuses a terminal, opens and accepts a diff, and verifies that a typing probe does not reach the previously opened editor. The integration test is built, launched through the editor test harness, and added to CI.
episode.diff: The behavioral implementation is a one-argument change in the shared diff-tab cleanup boundary: the matched tab is closed with keepFocus=true. Supporting changes add comprehensive unit coverage and a reusable editor mock, expose a development-only command for opening a diff during extension-host tests, bundle and launch the new integration tests, add the editor test dependency and scripts, and execute the suite in CI under a virtual display on Linux.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned resolution is commit e5b6680332883bd72aaa59292936b184f340256f, titled "fix(vscode-ide-companion): preserve terminal focus when closing diff tabs (#29378)", with parent 196c772a970166a26fa0e5f92f4fbd89ec265301.

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation closed a matched diff tab with close(tab), supplying no keep-focus argument.
The implementation changes the matched-tab close call from close(tab) to close(tab, true).

Before closing the tab, the shared routine clears the diff-visible context and removes tracked diff metadata and generated content; it then closes only the tab whose modified URI matches the requested diff URI, now with keepFocus=true.
Both accepting and cancelling a diff invoke the shared close routine; after cleanup they preserve their existing accepted or rejected protocol notifications for tracked diffs.
Closing a diff by original file path also resolves the tracked modified-document URI and invokes the same shared close routine.

Unit tests require direct close, accept, and cancel paths to call the tab-closing API with the matched tab and true, while also checking visibility reset, content cleanup, notifications, and missing-state behavior.

The extension-host regression test activates the extension, focuses a terminal, opens a diff, accepts it, sends a default typing command, and fails if the probe text appears in the previously opened dummy editor; absence of that text is the focus-preservation oracle.

A non-production command was added to open a diff with supplied file path and content, giving the extension-host regression test a controlled entry point without exposing that command in production mode.
The integration runner loads the focus test inside the extension host, and the launcher uses the editor test harness with other extensions disabled.
