title: Add a persistent policy for handing clicked links to the system browser
before: At first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, an ordinary HTTP(S) click handled by ExternalLink reached openLink and opened an in-app preview. The system browser was selected only for an explicit native request, the platform open-elsewhere modifier or middle click, connector authorization links, HUD links, and non-HTTP(S) schemes. There was no stored user preference or settings control that changed the ordinary-click destination.
after: At pinned merge 074349fb2744eacafbf80234444541aa736b1689, the desktop renderer owns an off-by-default, localStorage-backed boolean preference synchronized across open windows. A localized settings toggle changes that preference. The central clicked-link dispatcher consults it and, when enabled, sends normalized links through the existing operating-system browser bridge without creating an in-app preview. When disabled, prior routing remains intact. Explicit context-menu actions continue to invoke in-app preview or external handoff directly and are not overridden by the ordinary-click preference.
diff: Relative to first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, the merge changes 9 desktop files with 101 insertions and 1 deletion: it adds the preference store and its persistence/cross-window tests; adds a settings toggle plus typed English, Russian, and Chinese copy; imports the preference into the central link dispatcher and adds it to the external-handoff guard; and adds a component test proving that an enabled preference sends a plain web-link click externally and leaves the preview collection empty.

episode.title: Add a persistent policy for handing clicked links to the system browser
episode.before: At first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, an ordinary HTTP(S) click handled by ExternalLink reached openLink and opened an in-app preview. The system browser was selected only for an explicit native request, the platform open-elsewhere modifier or middle click, connector authorization links, HUD links, and non-HTTP(S) schemes. There was no stored user preference or settings control that changed the ordinary-click destination.
episode.after: At pinned merge 074349fb2744eacafbf80234444541aa736b1689, the desktop renderer owns an off-by-default, localStorage-backed boolean preference synchronized across open windows. A localized settings toggle changes that preference. The central clicked-link dispatcher consults it and, when enabled, sends normalized links through the existing operating-system browser bridge without creating an in-app preview. When disabled, prior routing remains intact. Explicit context-menu actions continue to invoke in-app preview or external handoff directly and are not overridden by the ordinary-click preference.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, the merge changes 9 desktop files with 101 insertions and 1 deletion: it adds the preference store and its persistence/cross-window tests; adds a settings toggle plus typed English, Russian, and Chinese copy; imports the preference into the central link dispatcher and adds it to the external-handoff guard; and adds a component test proving that an enabled preference sends a plain web-link click externally and leaves the preview collection empty.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned ref 074349fb2744eacafbf80234444541aa736b1689 is the merge of PR #120790, titled as a desktop setting to always open links in the external browser; its first parent is 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40.

The first-parent change comprises 9 desktop files, 101 insertions, and 1 deletion, including a new preference store, store tests, routing integration, routing tests, settings UI, and localization entries.

The new renderer-owned preference defaults to false, is stored under hermes.desktop.alwaysExternalLinks.v1, persists every atom update, and reacts to matching browser storage events so other open windows adopt the stored value.
Store tests assert the preference defaults off, persists both true and false transitions, and follows a matching storage event from another window.
The configuration settings surface subscribes to the preference and renders a ToggleRow whose change handler updates it.
The translation contract and English, Russian, and Chinese locales add a title and description explaining both ordinary-click external routing and the continuing explicit in-app-browser command.

The central openLink decision now reads the preference after URL normalization and before the existing authorization, HUD, and scheme guards; a true value selects openExternalLink, while a false value leaves the existing preview branch reachable.

ExternalLink intercepts ordinary anchor clicks, preserves consumer cancellation, derives an explicit native request from the component flag or modifier keys, and delegates the final destination decision to openLink.
In the first-parent version, the openLink external-routing guard did not consult any stored preference, so a normal HTTP(S) click fell through to the lazy in-app preview branch.

The pre-existing routing test establishes the baseline contract: a plain web-link click does not call the external bridge and instead creates an in-app preview; a modifier click calls the external bridge and creates no preview.
The added routing test enables the preference, performs a plain click, expects the operating-system bridge to receive the normalized URL, and expects the preview collection to remain empty.
Explicit context-menu choices bypass ordinary-click routing: Open in in-app browser calls openPreview directly, while Open in external browser calls openExternalLink directly.
Context-menu tests assert that both explicit destinations are offered for an ordinary chat link and that selecting Open in in-app browser creates a preview for the selected URL.
The desktop package declares Vitest as its test runner and exposes test and test:ui scripts suitable for executing the inspected store and component tests.

title: Route macOS workspace launches through an encoded application deep link
before: At parent commit 12c37a6b5cdb3fff2c03a355ca9948866bf1df07, the macOS launcher invoked `open -a <app_path> <workspace>`, passing the workspace as a macOS document-open argument. The resolution commit explains that recent desktop builds could focus the application without honoring that folder argument, so `codex app [PATH]` could fail to open the requested workspace.
after: At commit f94c49cf465b7403f22894f2db1432dee66fd64e, the launcher converts the workspace path into the `path` query parameter of a `codex://threads/new` URL using form URL encoding, then passes that URL to `open -a <app_path>`. Its failure message reports the same URL handed to the operating system. A unit test parses a deep link built from a path containing a space and `#` and confirms that the scheme, host, route, and decoded query value preserve the intended workspace.
diff: The single changed file, `codex-rs/cli/src/desktop_app/mac.rs`, adds `codex_new_thread_url`, which lossily converts the platform path to text, serializes it as a `path` query pair, and prefixes the query with `codex://threads/new?`. `open_codex_app` now constructs this URL and supplies it to the existing `open -a` subprocess instead of supplying the raw workspace path; the nonzero-exit diagnostic is updated accordingly. The same file adds `codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path`, covering URL parsing and query round-trip behavior for reserved characters. Existing upstream call sites still canonicalize the requested CLI path when possible and route both already-installed and newly-installed application launches through `open_codex_app`.

commit.subject: Use deep links for macOS codex app paths (#25485)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

`codex app [PATH]` is the documented CLI entry point for opening Codex
Desktop on a workspace. Recent desktop builds can focus the app while
failing to honor paths passed as macOS document-open arguments via `open
-a Codex.app <workspace>`, which broke `codex app .` for users. See
#25333; related report: #25166.

The desktop app still supports the explicit
`codex://threads/new?path=...` route, so the CLI should use that
app-owned launch surface instead of depending on folder-open event
delivery.

## What Changed

- Build a `codex://threads/new?path=<workspace>` URL in the macOS app
launcher.
- Pass that URL to `open -a <Codex.app>` instead of passing the
workspace path as a document argument.
- Add coverage that workspace paths needing escaping round-trip through
URL query encoding.

## Verification

- `just test -p codex-cli codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path`

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, `open_codex_app` passed the workspace path directly as the final argument to `open -a`, and its error diagnostic described that raw-path invocation.
The change replaces the raw workspace argument with a generated URL in both the subprocess invocation and nonzero-exit diagnostic.
The added URL builder serializes the workspace under the `path` query key with `url::form_urlencoded::Serializer` and returns the explicit `codex://threads/new` application route.

Both the existing-application branch and the install-then-launch branch pass their resolved application path and the requested workspace to the same `open_codex_app` boundary, so the deep-link handoff applies in either launch path.

The CLI `app` command accepts a workspace path, canonicalizes it when possible, and forwards it to the platform desktop-app launcher; the behavioral change therefore covers the documented `codex app [PATH]` entry point without changing its input contract.

The added unit test builds a deep link from `/tmp/codex workspace/#1`, parses it as a URL, and asserts scheme `codex`, host `threads`, path `/new`, and a decoded `path` query value exactly equal to the original workspace string.

The resolution commit records the focused verification command `just test -p codex-cli codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path`. The available bundle does not include CI status or captured command output.

candidate_workflows.name: replace-fragile-document-open-with-owned-deep-link
candidate_workflows.title: Replace an unreliable document-open handoff with an explicit application route
candidate_workflows.description: When an operating-system application launcher opens or focuses the correct application but loses the requested target, encode that target in a supported application-owned deep link and pass the link through the existing launch boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a CLI request to open a workspace reaches the selected desktop application with the exact target intact, including paths containing URL-reserved characters.
when_to_use: The operating-system launcher successfully selects or focuses the destination application but its generic document-open argument is not reliably honored.
The destination application provides a supported deep-link route capable of representing the requested target.
The target must survive transport through URL syntax without spaces, fragment markers, or other reserved characters changing its meaning.
anti_goals: Do not redesign application discovery, installation, architecture detection, or download behavior.
Do not shell-escape or concatenate the workspace into a URL manually when a structured query serializer is available.
Do not change the CLI workspace argument contract or optimize unrelated installer behavior.
Do not treat successful process launch alone as proof that the target was encoded or delivered correctly.
not_applicable_when: The destination application has no supported deep-link contract for the requested operation.
The failure is application discovery or process startup rather than loss of the target during handoff.
The target cannot be represented by the receiving application's textual URL contract without an explicitly accepted lossy conversion.
The platform launcher cannot pass URLs to the selected application.
inputs: Requested workspace path from the CLI entry point
Supported application deep-link scheme, authority, route, and query-key contract
Selected application bundle path
Operating-system application-launch command and exit status
workflow_graph.entry_state: The CLI has resolved a workspace and an application bundle, but the launch boundary passes the workspace as a generic document argument that may be ignored by the receiving application.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All existing application-launch branches hand a parseable, correctly encoded application-owned route to the platform launcher, and encoding tests prove that representative reserved characters round-trip to the original workspace value.

steps.condition: The receiving application exposes an explicit deep-link route for opening the requested target.
steps.validation: Parse the generated URL and verify its routing components and decoded target query value, including a path with a space and `#`.

steps.condition: The platform application launcher accepts the deep link as the application-open argument.
steps.validation: Confirm the launcher receives the generated link rather than the raw filesystem path, both pre-existing and newly-installed application branches reach this boundary, and nonzero exit status still produces an error containing the actual handoff target.

validation_ladder: Unit-test structured URL construction by parsing the result and asserting scheme, authority, route, and decoded query pairs.
Use a target containing URL-reserved characters to prove query serialization preserves target identity.
Inspect or spy on the operating-system command invocation to prove the encoded link, not the raw path, is handed off.
Exercise both the already-installed and install-then-launch call paths because both must converge on the corrected handoff.
On a supported platform with the desktop application available, run an end-to-end CLI launch and confirm the requested workspace is opened, not merely that the application is focused.
stop_conditions: Stop if the receiving application does not document or support an explicit route for the requested target.
Stop if URL parsing or query decoding does not reproduce the intended target.
Stop if any launch branch bypasses the corrected handoff boundary.
Stop if process success cannot be distinguished from successful target delivery; retain end-to-end validation as unresolved rather than claiming it.
unresolved_or_deferred: No CI status, review discussion, or captured output from the recorded focused test command is present in the evidence bundle.
The checkout and bundle establish URL construction and command wiring, but do not provide an automated assertion over the spawned `open` command arguments.
Actual end-to-end behavior in a recent macOS desktop build is not demonstrated by the available unit test.
The path conversion uses `to_string_lossy`; behavior for non-Unicode filesystem paths is not specified or tested by this change.

unresolved_questions: Did CI or a local run of `just test -p codex-cli codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path` pass? The commit records the command, but the supplied evidence contains no execution result.
Was the corrected launch verified end-to-end against an affected macOS desktop build, confirming that the requested workspace opens rather than only the application focusing?
Is lossy conversion of non-Unicode workspace paths an accepted part of the deep-link contract?

title: Replace repeated automatic browser launches with an explicit documentation handoff
before: At parent dca040908affc6277884514b4c726365359fd10b, the MCP status path detected an empty configured-and-blocked server set, then selected behavior by SANDBOX. Most environments awaited open(docsUrl), launching a browser tab and reporting that the documentation was being opened; sandbox environments instead returned the URL without launching it. Because the default `mcp` action delegates to the list action and both list and refresh call the same status function, repeated status requests with zero servers could repeatedly trigger this browser side effect.
after: At e7b468e122a29341a6e2e2ca67366e6d62014a6d, the empty-server branch has one environment-independent result: it returns an informational message containing the existing documentation URL and the internal `/docs` alternative. The browser-opening dependency and invocation are absent, so status requests no longer launch tabs while the documentation destination remains available for deliberate user handoff.
diff: The two-file change removes the `open` import, the SANDBOX conditional, and `await open(docsUrl)` from the status implementation. It replaces both prior messages with one deterministic informational response. The unit test removes the browser mock and the separate sandbox/non-sandbox cases, replacing them with one assertion for the unified response. Overall: 8 insertions and 39 deletions, with configured-server status handling unchanged by the shown diff.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure repeated empty-state status requests provide actionable documentation guidance without automatically opening browser tabs.
when_to_use: A command, status view, refresh path, or similarly repeatable interaction automatically opens documentation when no resources are configured.
Multiple callers converge on the same empty-state branch, making an otherwise helpful browser handoff repeatable.
The external documentation target should remain available, but navigation should require deliberate user action.
anti_goals: Do not remove or silently change the established documentation target.
Do not alter configured-resource status, discovery, authentication, or refresh behavior beyond the shared empty-state return path.
Do not optimize browser-launch mechanics or add another environment-specific automatic-launch policy.
Do not claim that the external URL destination or the internal documentation command itself was exercised unless separately validated.
not_applicable_when: Automatic browser navigation is the explicit primary operation requested by the user rather than an incidental empty-state side effect.
The path is guaranteed to execute only once and product requirements explicitly require immediate browser launch.
No stable link, internal route, or other actionable handoff can be supplied to the user.
The observed tab opening originates outside the inspected status-response boundary.
inputs: The empty-state predicate for the relevant resource collections.
All command or refresh call sites that reach the shared status-response boundary.
The existing external documentation target.
Any supported internal documentation route.
A command-level test fixture capable of producing the empty state.

workflow_graph.exit_state: Every inspected caller reaching the empty state receives the same actionable informational response; the preserved documentation target and internal alternative are visible, no automatic browser invocation remains in that branch, and a deterministic unit test guards the response contract.

steps.condition: Apply when the shared empty-state branch owns an incidental automatic browser handoff and must continue directing users to documentation.
steps.validation: The implementation has no browser-opener import or invocation for the empty state, preserves the documentation URL, supplies `/docs` as an alternative, and leaves non-empty status logic outside the diff.

steps.condition: Apply after the empty-state result has been made environment-independent.
steps.validation: With an empty configured-resource map, the command test asserts the exact informational handoff response without mocking or expecting a browser opener.

validation_ladder: Diff-level check: confirm removal of the external opener dependency, environment branch, and invocation while retaining the same documentation URL.
Call-site check: confirm default, list, and refresh status paths all converge on the repaired empty-state behavior.
Unit-contract check: produce the empty state and assert the exact informational response containing both the external URL and internal documentation route.
Broader regression check, when the checkout is runnable: execute the command test file and verify configured-resource status tests remain successful.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the empty-state predicate or its browser-launch side effect cannot be established from before-state code.
Stop if removing navigation would violate an explicit requirement that this interaction launch a browser.
Stop if preserving the link target or another actionable handoff is impossible.
Do not claim end-to-end link integrity or successful internal documentation routing without a separate oracle for those destinations.

The changed test verifies the returned URL text but does not resolve and inspect the shortened URL destination.
The changed test mentions `/docs` in the response but does not execute that command.
No runtime test execution result was established during this extraction; validation is grounded in the committed unit-test oracle and implementation diff.

candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution chain for removing unwanted automatic browser launches from a reusable empty-state status path while preserving link accessibility and establishing a deterministic regression oracle.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure repeated empty-state status requests provide actionable documentation guidance without automatically opening browser tabs.
when_to_use: A command, status view, refresh path, or similarly repeatable interaction automatically opens documentation when no resources are configured.
Multiple callers converge on the same empty-state branch, making an otherwise helpful browser handoff repeatable.
The external documentation target should remain available, but navigation should require deliberate user action.
anti_goals: Do not remove or silently change the established documentation target.
Do not alter configured-resource status, discovery, authentication, or refresh behavior beyond the shared empty-state return path.
Do not optimize browser-launch mechanics or add another environment-specific automatic-launch policy.
Do not claim that the external URL destination or the internal documentation command itself was exercised unless separately validated.
not_applicable_when: Automatic browser navigation is the explicit primary operation requested by the user rather than an incidental empty-state side effect.
The path is guaranteed to execute only once and product requirements explicitly require immediate browser launch.
No stable link, internal route, or other actionable handoff can be supplied to the user.
The observed tab opening originates outside the inspected status-response boundary.
inputs: The empty-state predicate for the relevant resource collections.
All command or refresh call sites that reach the shared status-response boundary.
The existing external documentation target.
Any supported internal documentation route.
A command-level test fixture capable of producing the empty state.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A repeatable shared status path automatically launches external documentation in at least one environment when its resource collections are empty, and its tests encode environment-specific opener behavior.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every inspected caller reaching the empty state receives the same actionable informational response; the preserved documentation target and internal alternative are visible, no automatic browser invocation remains in that branch, and a deterministic unit test guards the response contract.

steps.condition: Apply when the shared empty-state branch owns an incidental automatic browser handoff and must continue directing users to documentation.
steps.validation: The implementation has no browser-opener import or invocation for the empty state, preserves the documentation URL, supplies `/docs` as an alternative, and leaves non-empty status logic outside the diff.

steps.condition: Apply after the empty-state result has been made environment-independent.
steps.validation: With an empty configured-resource map, the command test asserts the exact informational handoff response without mocking or expecting a browser opener.

validation_ladder: Diff-level check: confirm removal of the external opener dependency, environment branch, and invocation while retaining the same documentation URL.
Call-site check: confirm default, list, and refresh status paths all converge on the repaired empty-state behavior.
Unit-contract check: produce the empty state and assert the exact informational response containing both the external URL and internal documentation route.
Broader regression check, when the checkout is runnable: execute the command test file and verify configured-resource status tests remain successful.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the empty-state predicate or its browser-launch side effect cannot be established from before-state code.
Stop if removing navigation would violate an explicit requirement that this interaction launch a browser.
Stop if preserving the link target or another actionable handoff is impossible.
Do not claim end-to-end link integrity or successful internal documentation routing without a separate oracle for those destinations.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle contains no PR body, review discussion, status checks, or reported test-run result.
The changed test verifies the returned URL text but does not resolve and inspect the shortened URL destination.
The changed test mentions `/docs` in the response but does not execute that command.
No runtime test execution result was established during this extraction; validation is grounded in the committed unit-test oracle and implementation diff.

unresolved_questions: Did CI or a local run execute the changed test successfully? The available GitHub bundle does not include status checks, and this extraction does not claim a runtime result.
Does `https://goo.gle/gemini-cli-docs-mcp` resolve to the intended live documentation destination? The implementation preserves the target, but the changed test only checks its literal presence.
Does the `/docs` command lead to the intended MCP documentation from this context? The change offers it as an alternative but adds no behavioral test for that route.

call_sites: The default `mcp` action delegates to the list action; the list action calls the shared status function, and refresh calls it after rediscovery. Therefore the empty-server branch governs multiple user-triggered status paths.
tests: Parent tests mocked the browser opener and separately asserted that sandbox execution did not open the URL while ordinary execution did open it.
The pinned test invokes the default command with an empty server map and asserts the exact unified informational response containing both the documentation URL and `/docs` guidance.

title: Extend package installation and validation through Python 3.14 across Linux and Windows
before: At first parent 265d8a473b5d5bf001db321b251674a120ad75da, package metadata admitted Python >=3.10,<3.13 and advertised classifiers only through 3.12. Linux and Windows source-test and published-package-check matrices covered 3.10-3.12. Base dependency inputs used a single scipy<1.16 constraint, the help input used numpy<2, and the generated base requirements pinned NumPy 1.26.4 and SciPy 1.15.3 without interpreter-specific alternatives or the Python 3.13+ audioop compatibility package.
after: At merge commit 861a1e4d154f268547a06497cc380e5a5dc8483a, package metadata admits Python >=3.10,<3.15 and advertises 3.13 and 3.14. Dedicated compatibility inputs select NumPy and SciPy ranges by interpreter version and add audioop-lts for Python >=3.13; the compilation pipeline preserves these markers in the generated base requirements instead of replacing them with one resolved pin. The help dependency input is aligned with the new NumPy split and explicitly requires a compatible Torch floor. Linux and Windows source-test matrices and published-package installation checks cover every supported interpreter from 3.10 through 3.14.
diff: The implementation changed 15 files with 56 insertions and 42 deletions. It widened requires-python and classifiers; added requirements/python-compat.in and requirements/pydub.in; included the compatibility input from the base requirements; changed the compilation post-processing to remove resolved tree-sitter, NumPy, and SciPy pins before appending maintained marker-based compatibility inputs; regenerated base, common, browser, development, and help requirement artifacts; and expanded four Linux/Windows CI matrices from 3.10-3.12 to 3.10-3.14. No repository test file was changed, and the evidence bundle contains no status-check results.

candidate_atomics.title: Partition dependency constraints by runtime capability
candidate_atomics.description: Replace universal dependency pins with environment-marked ranges and add a conditional compatibility backport where newer interpreters removed a required standard-library facility.

semantic_action.intent: Keep one package installable across old and new interpreter releases whose binary dependency support and standard-library facilities differ.

semantic_action.post_state: Environment markers select dependency ranges compatible with each interpreter cohort, and the compatibility backport is installed only on runtimes that need it.
semantic_action.validation: Resolve or inspect requirements under representatives on both sides of each marker boundary and confirm exactly one compatible NumPy range, one compatible SciPy range, and conditional audioop-lts selection; the committed generated requirements expose these marker branches.

candidate_atomics.title: Preserve runtime markers in generated release requirements
candidate_atomics.description: Reconcile resolver output with maintained compatibility inputs so a lock generated on one host does not collapse cross-runtime alternatives into host-specific unconditional pins.

semantic_action.intent: Produce distributable requirements whose dependency choices remain valid across the full supported interpreter range.

semantic_action.post_state: The generated base requirements omit host-resolved assignments for compatibility-sensitive packages and contain the maintained marker-based alternatives plus the conditional backport.
semantic_action.validation: Run the compilation pipeline, then assert that the final base requirements contain the marker-based alternatives and no unconditional NumPy or SciPy assignment; the committed script and regenerated artifact demonstrate this transformation.

candidate_workflows.name: extend-cross-platform-package-runtime-support
candidate_workflows.title: Extend a packaged application across new interpreter releases
candidate_workflows.description: Coordinate metadata, runtime-sensitive dependency policy, generated release artifacts, and Linux/Windows validation when adding interpreter versions whose dependency availability differs from older supported versions.

workflow_graph.goal: Make source and released-package installation support the expanded interpreter range on Linux and Windows without breaking dependency resolution for older supported interpreters.
when_to_use: Package metadata must admit one or more new interpreter releases.
At least one dependency or removed standard-library module requires different treatment across old and new interpreter cohorts.
The repository commits generated dependency artifacts and validates installation on multiple operating systems.
anti_goals: Do not drop an older supported interpreter merely to use one unconditional modern dependency pin.
Do not claim runtime support solely by changing package classifiers or the interpreter upper bound.
Do not let a lock generated on one host replace cross-runtime marker branches with host-specific pins.
Do not broaden unrelated application behavior or optimize dependency versions beyond what compatibility requires.
not_applicable_when: The project distributes no Python package or does not declare interpreter compatibility.
All supported runtimes resolve the same dependency set and no generated artifact can collapse environment-specific choices.
The requested interpreter is unavailable in the target CI platforms or required dependencies have no viable compatible release or backport.

Package metadata and classifiers
Direct and transitive dependency compatibility by interpreter
Generated-requirements compilation pipeline
Supported operating-system CI workflows
Source-test and published-package installation oracles

workflow_graph.exit_state: Metadata, dependency policy, generated artifacts, source-test matrices, and published-package checks consistently cover Python 3.10-3.14 on Linux and Windows, with runtime markers preserving older-interpreter compatibility.

steps.condition: Release dependencies are generated through a resolver that can emit host-specific unconditional pins.
steps.validation: Regenerated release requirements retain marker branches and contain no conflicting unconditional assignments for compatibility-sensitive packages.

steps.condition: The repository supports Linux and Windows and publishes an installable package.
steps.validation: Every supported interpreter has Linux and Windows source-install/test jobs and published-package installation/version-check jobs.

validation_ladder: Statically verify that metadata bounds and classifiers agree on Python 3.10-3.14.
Regenerate dependency artifacts and verify that compatibility-sensitive packages retain mutually exclusive runtime markers without unconditional conflicting pins.
Install the source package and run pytest for every supported interpreter on Linux and Windows.
Install the published package for every supported interpreter on Linux and Windows and compare its reported version with the latest release tag.
Require observed CI status results before treating configured workflow coverage as proven execution success.
stop_conditions: Stop if any newly admitted interpreter has no viable dependency set or required compatibility backport.
Stop if generated artifacts cannot preserve the runtime-specific policy without conflicting assignments.
Stop promotion if either operating-system family lacks source-install/test coverage for a claimed supported runtime.
Defer success claims when CI execution or release-install results are unavailable.

title: Add an architecture-specific Windows release artifact across build, packaging, and publication
before: At first parent ac75abee43cc2b3ebbaf616b98a5c5a9c51b804d, the release builder's default target matrix contained macOS ARM64/x64, Linux ARM64/x64, and Windows x64. Only Windows x64 received a .exe name, the win32_x64 koffi native module, ZIP packaging, ZIP extraction, and release upload. The CI workflow used Bun 1.2.20.
after: At pinned merge 93708de65d34ecceb2b86f626d18c2df356bd70c, the default matrix also builds Windows ARM64 using Bun 1.3.10, installs its clipboard and image native dependencies, emits pi.exe, selects and copies koffi's win32_arm64 module, creates and extracts pi-windows-arm64.zip, and includes that archive in both release creation and fallback upload. title: Restore the desktop packaging toolchain in isolated installer stages and report missing prerequisites as failure
before: At parent commit 77bb64813cb987ad80236219a20c6cb549b40049, the explicitly requested desktop stage entered the checkout and called the desktop builder without first restoring the managed Node directory to PATH. Because each stage ran in a separate process, npm could be absent even when Node had been provisioned earlier. The builder treated that condition as a successful skip by warning and returning 0, allowing the stage protocol to emit an ok result despite producing no desktop application.
after: At fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f, the desktop stage calls the Node prerequisite resolver before invoking the builder. The builder also retries prerequisite resolution when npm is absent and returns 1 with remediation guidance if npm remains unavailable. That nonzero result flows through the existing stage protocol as a failed JSON result, while successful builds continue to require a recognized desktop application artifact.
diff: The single-file change to scripts/install.sh adds 17 lines and removes 2. It inserts check_node into the desktop stage, replaces the missing-npm warning and successful return with a self-provisioning attempt followed by an explicit error and return 1, and documents why an explicitly requested desktop package must not silently degrade. No test file was changed.

commit.subject: fix(install): build desktop in 'desktop' stage on macOS/Linux instead of silently skipping (#36134)
commit.body_excerpt:
The thin installer (apps/bootstrap-installer) drives install.sh stage-by-stage,
each in its own process. The `desktop` stage never called check_node, so the
Hermes-managed Node provisioned earlier (at $HERMES_HOME/node/bin) wasn't on
PATH. install_desktop's `command -v npm` check then failed and the build was
skipped — yet the stage still reported {"ok":true,"skipped":false}, so the
installer showed "Installation Complete" and only failed at the end with
"Couldn't find a built Hermes desktop ... the desktop build step may have been
skipped or failed."

Fix:
- Call check_node in the `desktop` stage (mirrors every other Node-dependent
  stage) so the managed Node is on PATH (or installed).
- Make install_desktop self-provision via check_node and hard-fail (return 1)
  if npm is still unavailable, instead of a silent `return 0`. The desktop
  stage only runs when a build is explicitly requested (--include-desktop), so
  an unavailable toolchain is a real failure, not graceful degradation.

Verified on macOS arm64: the `desktop` stage now builds
release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app, which matches resolve_hermes_desktop_exe, so the
installer's "Launch Hermes" succeeds.

when_to_use: Installer stages run in separate processes or otherwise do not inherit PATH mutations from prerequisite stages.
A packaging stage depends on a runtime that may have been installed into an application-managed directory.
The current behavior can skip a requested build and still report successful completion.

not_applicable_when: All stages execute in one process with guaranteed environment inheritance and the prerequisite is already enforced at the packaging boundary.

The failure is caused by the package build itself or an unrecognized output path rather than prerequisite discovery.

Stage result protocol that maps exit status to success or failure
Expected output artifact paths

before: At parent commit 55db3c776c86798938ccf386f53b1d5593c37468, the release action built the workspace packages and generated the root bundle, but the public npm CLI publish path did not stage that bundle inside packages/cli or rewrite the CLI manifest for a self-contained bundled artifact. packages/cli/package.json still published files from dist, pointed the gemini executable and main entry to dist/index.js, and retained workspace/runtime dependencies, development dependencies, scripts, and release-time configuration.

evidence_units.claim: In the parent state, packages/cli/package.json allowed only dist, mapped gemini and main to dist/index.js, and contained runtime dependencies, devDependencies, scripts, and config.
The release action already runs `npm run bundle` before package publication, establishing the root bundle as an input available to the newly added preparation step.
The root manifest supplies optional native packages for multiple operating-system and architecture variants, including Darwin, Linux, and Windows node-pty packages, plus keytar and node-pty.

The preparation script resolves bundle at the release working directory, fails with exit status 1 when it is absent, otherwise removes any prior packages/cli/bundle and recursively copies the generated bundle into that package directory.

The preparation script clones root optionalDependencies, removes gemini-cli-devtools defensively, changes the CLI package files allowlist to bundle/, maps the gemini executable to bundle/gemini.js, deletes dependencies, devDependencies, scripts, main, and config, then assigns the filtered optional dependencies and writes the manifest.
The release action invokes the preparation script after core installation and before the CLI token and `npm publish` steps, only when the target registry is not GitHub Packages.
The implementation provides a local precondition oracle: preparation cannot continue without a generated root bundle and emits an instruction to run `npm run bundle` before exiting unsuccessfully.

The release pipeline's existing CLI publication command supports dry-run mode and consumes the package only after the manifest and bundle preparation step, providing the nearest encoded packaging-level validation point, although the evidence bundle contains no status-check result.

No test or specification file changed in the pinned commit, and the supplied bundle explicitly records `no_test_file_change_observed`; therefore no automated regression oracle specific to the new preparation script is established by this episode.

title: Redact secrets at terminal exception-result and ACP stderr boundaries
before: At parent commit 2a743e5f4377419c54054ce7c65c79cff98a092c, terminal_tool serialized raw exception text and traceback.format_exc() into model-visible JSON for both the generic exception handler and the TERMINAL_DEGRADED_MODE=fail branch. ACP logging setup also replaced root handlers with a stderr handler using plain logging.Formatter, so that independently configured diagnostic surface bypassed the repository's redacting formatter.
after: At commit 72eda946be949a5932923df3325037a0d6c5da49, both terminal error-result branches apply redact_sensitive_text to the error and traceback fields before JSON serialization, preserving the structured failure response while masking secrets. ACP stderr setup uses RedactingFormatter, causing formatted log records on that handler to pass through the shared secret-redaction policy.
diff: The implementation changes two diagnostic emission boundaries without changing the redaction algorithm: tools/terminal_tool.py adds lazy imports of redact_sensitive_text and sanitizes four outgoing field values across two exception paths; acp_adapter/entry.py replaces logging.Formatter with RedactingFormatter. Two regression-test modules add three tests that inject prefixed secrets and assert that secret values are absent while useful context and response structure remain. The commit reports 98 insertions and 5 deletions across four files.

commit.subject: fix(security): redact terminal exception results and ACP stderr logs (#77484)
commit.body_excerpt:
Closes the last two emission gaps from #77484:

- tools/terminal_tool.py: both exception paths (generic except and
  TERMINAL_DEGRADED_MODE=fail) returned raw str(e) + traceback.format_exc()
  to the model — only the logger copy was redacted. Exception text can
  embed the failing command line and any secrets inline in it; both fields
  now pass through redact_sensitive_text.
- acp_adapter/entry.py: _setup_logging cleared root handlers and installed
  a plain logging.Formatter, bypassing redaction entirely on ACP stderr.
  Now uses RedactingFormatter like every other logging surface.

The other three gaps from #77484 (process(list), *_KEY regex variants,
control-char splits) were fixed in #80964/#80965.

candidate_workflows.name: close-secret-leaks-across-diagnostic-emission-boundaries
candidate_workflows.title: Close secret leaks at structured-result and log-output boundaries
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for applying an existing redaction policy to diagnostic surfaces that bypass it: sanitize exception-derived fields immediately before structured return, and attach the shared formatter to independently configured log handlers, then verify secrecy and retained diagnostic utility at each boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure that secrets embedded in exception diagnostics or log records cannot cross the affected consumer-facing diagnostic boundaries while structured errors and useful non-secret context remain intact.
when_to_use: A structured error result exposes raw exception messages, tracebacks, command context, or comparable diagnostic text to an external consumer.
A subsystem replaces inherited logging handlers or formatters and therefore bypasses an established application-wide redaction formatter.
An existing, tested sensitive-text redaction policy can be reused at the emission boundary.
anti_goals: Do not remove the error result, traceback field, log destination, log layout, filters, or status information merely to avoid leakage.
Do not redesign or broaden the secret-detection algorithm when the demonstrated defect is an emission boundary that fails to invoke the existing policy.
Do not claim closure of unrelated secret-emission gaps outside the inspected exception-result and ACP stderr surfaces.
not_applicable_when: The diagnostic text is already demonstrably redacted after all formatting and immediately before emission.
No trusted redaction function or formatter exists and its detection behavior cannot be established from implementation and tests.
The data must remain byte-exact for an authorized internal-only consumer and applying this redactor would violate that explicit contract.
inputs: Inventory of externally visible diagnostic-result fields and independently configured log handlers
Existing sensitive-text redaction function and redacting log formatter
Representative secret-bearing exceptions and log records
Branch controls needed to reach each affected exception path
Test runner capable of executing the focused regression tests
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least one externally observable diagnostic path emits exception-derived or log-formatted text without applying the shared redaction policy at its final boundary.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All evidenced diagnostic paths apply the shared redaction policy immediately before structured serialization or during final log formatting, and focused tests demonstrate that raw secrets are absent while response structure and useful context are retained.

steps.condition: Required for each structured exception-result branch that can contain exception-derived secret material.
steps.validation: Exercise the generic and configured degraded-fail branches; verify the secret is absent from error and traceback while status and useful failure context remain.

steps.condition: Required when the subsystem clears or replaces inherited handlers and assigns its own formatter.
steps.validation: Format a secret-bearing record through the installed handler; verify the raw value is absent and the non-secret key label remains.

validation_ladder: Static comparison: confirm each raw emission point in the parent is replaced by the shared redaction function or formatter without changing unrelated routing and response structure.
Branch-level structured-result tests: inject a secret-bearing generic exception and a degraded-fail connection exception, then inspect every returned diagnostic field.
Sink-level logging test: format a secret-bearing record through the exact handler installed by subsystem logging setup.
Integration check: run the three focused regression tests together in an environment with the repository's test dependencies.
Broader regression check: run the surrounding terminal-tool, ACP-adapter, and redaction test suites to detect formatting, filtering, or response-contract regressions.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the parent and after states do not identify a concrete unredacted emission boundary.
Stop if redaction is applied only to an internal logger copy while another consumer-facing copy remains raw.
Stop if the focused tests do not assert both secret absence and preservation of the required diagnostic contract.
Do not report runtime validation as passed when the test runner or dependencies are unavailable.

Stop logging response headers on successful WebSocket connections and payload
previews for tool calls. Keep the connection URL, tool name, and thread ID in
their respective log entries.

candidate_workflows.title: Remove sensitive values from routine diagnostics while preserving operational context
candidate_workflows.description: Audit each information-level diagnostic at a successful transport or invocation boundary, remove broad metadata or argument serialization, retain only identifiers needed to understand the event, and confirm that the underlying protocol and execution paths still consume the original data normally.

workflow_graph.goal: Routine successful-connection and tool-invocation diagnostics no longer expose response metadata or tool arguments, while retaining event identity and unchanged operational behavior.
when_to_use: An info-level success or invocation message serializes a complete metadata collection or request/tool argument payload.
The sensitive value is needed by runtime processing but is not required to identify the diagnostic event.
The diagnostic can remain useful with bounded identifiers such as a connection target, correlation ID, or operation name.
anti_goals: Do not disable successful-connection or tool-invocation diagnostics entirely.
Do not remove metadata or payloads from protocol processing, persistence, or tool execution.
Do not broaden the change to error diagnostics, payload storage, or unrelated telemetry without separate evidence and validation.
Do not optimize diagnostic verbosity or performance beyond eliminating the sensitive formatting operations.
not_applicable_when: The allegedly sensitive value is not emitted by the diagnostic boundary.
The full value is an explicitly required, access-controlled audit record with a documented retention contract.
Removing the value would also remove it from runtime behavior because logging and processing are inseparably coupled and cannot first be separated.
Only issue-title or classification evidence is available and the actual before/after logging expressions cannot be inspected.
inputs: Pinned implementation and parent refs
Locations of routine diagnostics that serialize metadata or arguments
Classification of identifiers that must remain for operational usefulness
Call sites and downstream consumers of the original metadata or payload
A source comparison or log-capture oracle capable of detecting forbidden values

workflow_graph.exit_state: Successful connection logs contain the connection URL without response headers, and tool-call logs contain the thread ID and tool name without argument previews; connection metadata handling and tool execution remain intact.

steps.validation: The changed success message has no response-metadata formatting expression, retains the connection identifier, and is followed by unchanged status and selected-metadata processing.

steps.condition: Apply when a routine invocation diagnostic derives or formats a preview from tool arguments.
steps.validation: The changed invocation branch neither derives nor formats an argument preview, retains the correlation field and tool name, and still persists and dispatches the call.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent state to identify the exact metadata and payload expressions copied into routine logs.
Inspect the implementation diff to confirm only the sensitive formatting and now-unused import or local value were removed.
Verify the remaining messages retain the intended connection, correlation, and operation identifiers.
Trace downstream code to confirm response metadata is still consumed for protocol behavior and the original tool call is still persisted and executed.
Run focused log-capture tests with sentinel header and tool-argument values when such a harness is available; assert sentinels are absent and retained identifiers are present.
Run the affected transport and core test suites or compile checks to detect behavioral or unused-import regressions.
stop_conditions: Stop if the before-state diagnostic cannot be established from source or captured output.
Stop if removing the formatted value also changes connection negotiation, response metadata interpretation, persistence, or tool execution.
Stop and separate the work if additional diagnostic boundaries have different sensitivity contracts or validation oracles.
Do not claim runtime log-redaction coverage until a log-capture test or equivalent execution oracle has been run.

The evidence bundle does not provide CI or status-check results, and no test execution result is attributable to the pinned commit.
The change intentionally retains connection URLs, thread identifiers, and tool names; whether those identifiers require further masking is outside the evidenced scope.

limitations: No fabricated GitHub discussion metadata; implementation evidence must come from local git and checkout.

episode.title: Honor the telemetry payload-consent flag across diagnostic logging paths
episode.before: At parent commit dce13019b9e43b253d03e7fb2c12550cdd94e0aa, ordinary telemetry records emitted request_text, response_text, tool function_args, and complete tool metadata without consulting getTelemetryLogPromptsEnabled(). Policy-generation and verdict diagnostics likewise sent prompts, trusted content, generated policy, tool-call text, and verdict rationale through both OpenTelemetry and Clearcut regardless of that flag, although some semantic GenAI payload logging was already gated separately.
episode.after: At commit 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e, payload-bearing request, response, tool-call, policy-generation, and verdict attributes are added only when getTelemetryLogPromptsEnabled() is true. With the flag false, tool metadata is reduced to an explicit allowlist of aggregate line/character counters, while operational fields such as function name, verdict result, and errors remain available. The policy diagnostics apply the same rule to both OpenTelemetry and Clearcut.
episode.diff: The change modifies four telemetry files (437 insertions and 57 deletions): event serialization in types.ts now conditionally emits request_text, response_text, function_args, policy inputs/outputs, tool-call text, and rationale; tool metadata is filtered through eight explicitly safe aggregate keys and JSON-serialized; conseca-logger.ts conditionally constructs Clearcut sensitive-field entries while retaining verdict and error entries; tests add enabled/disabled assertions for API response text, API request text, tool arguments, and policy-generation/verdict fields across OpenTelemetry and Clearcut.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e is titled “Respect logPrompts flag for logging sensitive fields (#26153)”, has parent dce13019b9e43b253d03e7fb2c12550cdd94e0aa, and changes four telemetry implementation/test files.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, and changed_files_name_status

evidence_units.claim: In the parent, ToolCallEvent always placed serialized function_args and complete metadata in OpenTelemetry attributes; ApiRequestEvent always placed request_text there; ApiResponseEvent included response_text whenever present.
evidence_units.source: git show dce13019b9e43b253d03e7fb2c12550cdd94e0aa:packages/core/src/telemetry/types.ts, ToolCallEvent.toOpenTelemetryAttributes, ApiRequestEvent.toLogRecord, and ApiResponseEvent.toLogRecord

evidence_units.claim: In the parent, policy-generation OpenTelemetry attributes always included user_prompt, trusted_content, and policy, while verdict attributes always included user_prompt, policy, tool_call, verdict, and verdict_rationale.

The implementation gates tool arguments, API request text, API response text, policy-generation payloads, and verdict payloads on config.getTelemetryLogPromptsEnabled(), while leaving non-payload event attributes outside the conditional blocks.

When prompt logging is disabled, ToolCallEvent filters metadata to eight aggregate model/user added-or-removed line/character counters; when enabled it preserves all metadata, and it emits metadata only when the resulting object is nonempty.

The general telemetry logger passes Config into event record serializers, making the runtime prompt-logging preference available at the final OpenTelemetry attribute-construction boundary used by API and tool-call logging.
evidence_units.source: git show 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e:packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.ts; logApiRequest, logApiResponse, and logToolCall calls to event record/attribute serializers, corroborated by packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts

evidence_units.claim: The policy diagnostic logger now builds Clearcut data conditionally: payload entries are appended only when prompt logging is enabled, while verdict result and error entries remain unconditional; OpenTelemetry uses the correspondingly gated event serializers.
Logger tests assert that request_text and response_text are absent when prompt logging is disabled, and that response_text is present when it is enabled.
evidence_units.source: git show 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e:packages/core/src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts, API request semantic-log disabled case and logApiResponse logPrompts cases

evidence_units.claim: Tool-call tests assert that function_args is absent while function_name remains when prompt logging is disabled, and that serialized function_args is present when the flag is enabled.

Policy diagnostic tests assert disabled-mode omission of user prompt, trusted content, policy, tool call, and rationale from OpenTelemetry and Clearcut, retention of verdict/error fields, and enabled-mode inclusion of sensitive fields.
evidence_units.source: git show 2194da2b0213fa39062302ea3a2ee75ef768648e:packages/core/src/telemetry/conseca-logger.test.ts, added logPrompts enabled/disabled cases

evidence_units.claim: The added tests exercise both consent states and verify selective retention rather than disabling whole events: event name, function name, verdict result, and errors remain observable while payload fields are omitted.
The evidence bundle identifies PR/issue 26153 as a verified implementation-plus-test training candidate but reports that the issue body, discussion, reviews, and status checks are unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: gate-diagnostic-payload-fields
candidate_atomics.title: Gate diagnostic payload fields on explicit logging consent
candidate_atomics.description: At the final event-serialization boundary, omit free-form request, response, prompt, policy, tool-argument, tool-call, and rationale fields unless payload logging is explicitly enabled, while preserving non-payload operational attributes.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent user or model content from entering diagnostic records when payload logging has been disabled without suppressing the entire operational event.
semantic_action.pre_state: A diagnostic event contains free-form payload fields, and its serializer can access a runtime setting that expresses whether such payloads may be logged.
semantic_action.post_state: Payload fields are absent when consent is disabled and present when enabled; non-payload event identity, status, timing, and routing fields remain independently observable.
semantic_action.validation: Serialize representative API and tool events under both flag values; assert payload-key absence in disabled mode, payload-key presence in enabled mode, and retention of non-payload keys such as event name or function name.

candidate_atomics.name: allowlist-safe-aggregate-metadata
candidate_atomics.title: Reduce mixed diagnostic metadata to explicitly safe aggregates
candidate_atomics.description: When a metadata container can mix content-bearing values with harmless counters, retain only a small explicit allowlist of aggregate measurements while payload logging is disabled.

semantic_action.intent: Keep useful quantitative diagnostics without leaking arbitrary nested metadata that may contain user-derived content.
semantic_action.pre_state: A diagnostic metadata map may contain both approved aggregate counters and arbitrary or content-bearing keys, and payload logging is disabled.
semantic_action.post_state: Only explicitly approved aggregate keys remain; an empty sanitized map is not emitted, while enabled mode preserves the original metadata map.
semantic_action.validation: Serialize a metadata map containing approved counters and an unapproved nested value under disabled mode and assert that only approved keys remain; repeat under enabled mode and assert that the full map is preserved.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-redaction-across-telemetry-sinks
candidate_atomics.title: Apply the same payload boundary across telemetry sinks
candidate_atomics.description: Enforce the same consent decision in each backend-specific representation while retaining safe verdict and error diagnostics.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid a privacy bypass in which one diagnostic backend redacts sensitive fields but another backend still transmits them.
semantic_action.pre_state: One logical event is emitted to multiple telemetry sinks whose payloads are constructed through separate code paths.
semantic_action.post_state: Every sink omits the same sensitive payload categories when consent is disabled, while safe outcome and error fields continue to be emitted.
semantic_action.validation: Emit policy-generation and verdict events to each configured sink with the flag disabled and enabled; compare backend payloads for omission/inclusion and verify that verdict and error fields survive disabled mode.

candidate_workflows.name: enforce-consent-aware-diagnostic-redaction
candidate_workflows.title: Enforce consent-aware redaction at diagnostic emission boundaries
candidate_workflows.description: Identify content-bearing diagnostic fields, guard direct payload attributes, sanitize mixed metadata, reconcile all sink-specific encodings, and validate both privacy and retained observability.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure disabling payload logging removes sensitive or content-bearing values from every diagnostic representation while preserving useful non-sensitive operational telemetry.
when_to_use: A runtime privacy or consent flag is intended to control prompt, response, command, policy, rationale, or comparable free-form diagnostic payloads.
The same logical event is serialized through multiple record types or telemetry backends.
Structured metadata may combine safe aggregate measurements with arbitrary content-bearing values.
anti_goals: Do not disable all telemetry when only payload content requires suppression.
Do not remove safe event identity, timing, status, verdict, error, or aggregate measurement fields solely because payload logging is disabled.
Do not treat an entire extensible metadata object as safe merely because some of its current keys are numeric counters.

commit.subject: fix(qqbot): security hardening — gateway validation, atomic state, sanitized logging (#6200)
commit.body_excerpt:
* fix(qqbot): validate gateway URL protocol to prevent SSRF

- Add validateGatewayUrl(): enforce wss:// protocol, warn on unexpected hostnames
- Integrate into fetchGatewayUrl() return path
- Truncate error body in fetchAccessToken() to 80 chars
- Add 6 tests covering protocol rejection, wss acceptance, and edge cases

* fix(qqbot): atomic state persistence and error log sanitization

State persistence hardening:
- Atomic saveQQState() via tmp+renameSync with disposed guard and unref()
- Atomic flushQQState() with {mode: 0o600} permissions
- Entry type validation in restoreQQState() for chatTypeMap and msgSeqMap

Error log sanitization:
- Wrap all user-controlled data in process.stderr.write() with sanitizeLogText()
- Covering: connect retry, sendMessage errors, state persistence failures,
  token refresh, malformed gateway, WebSocket errors, reconnect, and
  C2C/group handler error paths

* fix(qqbot): add replyMsgId validation in restoreQQState()

Add type/length validation for replyMsgId entries when restoring from
persisted state, consistent with the existing chatTypeMap and msgSeqMap
input validation filters. Entries must be strings ≤ 128 chars.

* fix(qqbot): add test coverag

title: Add a transactional SQLite session backend with schema-backed summaries and bounded context reconstruction
before: At parent 54fad505b9d8cbc8922ff55d7e2938f70cbf6a3d, the harness exposed only in-memory and JSONL session storage behavior. SessionStorage required a full getPathToRoot traversal and unpaged getEntries; Session derived the session name by scanning entries and had no storage-level statistics contract. There was no SQLite schema, migration runner, transactional relational backend, branch materialization, or persisted summary cache.
after: At 9e7582aa03e54f410fa9688197a3b64514e93400, SessionStorage exposes storage-owned name/stat queries, cursor-based entry retrieval, and a path query bounded by the latest compaction. Appending an entry updates the event row, sequence, active leaf, branch membership, and materialized state in one database transaction, with in-memory state restored if the transaction fails. diff: The change extends the shared session schema and storage interface; updates memory and JSONL implementations and Session call sites; stores retained compaction messages and stops ancestry traversal at a self-contained compaction; adds a node:sqlite adapter, database abstraction, migration loader, initial relational schema, repository lifecycle, entry encoding, branch indexes, ordered sequences, and materialized summaries; and adds or expands tests for schema creation, metadata round trips, active-leaf and branch consistency, reopen behavior, entry paging, resource cleanup, transactional rollback, aggregate consistency, retained-tail context reconstruction, and named SQLite parameters.

commit.subject: feat: sqlite session storage (#6594)
commit.body_excerpt:
This PR:

- Adds retainedTail to compaction entries in the new agent harness so we don't have to walk up the tree for the 2000 tokens before compaction,
- Changes getPathToRoot to getPathToRootOrCompaction to only load until last compaction, as unnecessary to access all nodes where it is called,
- Adds a SQLite storage backend, in a separate packages/session-backend-sqlite, with a migration system and schemas as per on-site discussions: sessions to match session header messages (except for metadata, which I couldn't understand what it's used for or where it gets written, so I omitted it), session_entries for shared entry types as columns plus payload as a json for what remains, session_sequences to represent the append-only, serialized nature of the jsonl files, branch_entries to attribute nodes to branches (relationship one-to-many), and session_materialized with the session info (see /session in TUI) to act as a "cache" or quick-access for costs, message count, token info, labels, session name, and model-thinking-level config (e.g. for fast resume).
- This is compatible with the new agent harness Session abstraction.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 9e7582aa03e54f410fa9688197a3b64514e93400 with parent 54fad505b9d8cbc8922ff55d7e2938f70cbf6a3d; its subject is "feat: sqlite session storage (#6594)" and it changes implementation and tests across the agent and new SQLite package.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --name-status 9e7582aa03e54f410fa9688197a3b64514e93400; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: The parent SessionStorage contract had getPathToRoot and unparameterized getEntries, while the implementation ref adds getSessionName, getSessionStats, getPathToRootOrCompaction, and cursor options for getEntries.
Session delegates name and statistics queries to storage, accepts entry cursor options, and uses the bounded path operation for branch loading; fork preparation also uses the bounded path operation.

The initial SQLite migration defines tables for sessions, ordered session entries, per-session sequences, branch membership, session summaries, and entry-level materialized values, plus indexes for chronology, parent lookup, type lookup, and branch lookup.
The migration runner creates a migrations ledger, loads ordered SQL files, skips recorded migrations, and applies each unrecorded migration and its ledger insertion in a transaction.

SQLite appendEntry encodes and inserts the event, advances its sequence, updates materialized summary state, stores entry materializations, updates active leaf state, and reconciles branch membership inside one transaction; on failure it restores the prior in-memory summary, entry cache, leaf, and active-branch state.

The materialized-state reducer derives normalized session name, labels, message count, token and cost totals, current model, and thinking level from appended entries, including usage from assistant messages, compactions, and branch summaries.

SQLite active branches are explicitly materialized by ordered entry sequence; active-branch reads reconstruct entries from branch membership while excluding leaf-navigation marker entries from model context.

Compaction preparation now captures retained recent messages, the harness persists them on the compaction entry, and context reconstruction emits the summary plus retainedTail; legacy entries without retainedTail continue to use firstKeptEntryId.
Memory, JSONL, and SQLite path walkers stop at a compaction carrying retainedTail, or walk only as far as firstKeptEntryId for a legacy compaction, rather than necessarily reaching the root.

SQLite tests assert migration recording and expected tables, metadata persistence through create/list/open/fork, transactional active-leaf materialization, distinct branch materialization after a fork, reopen from materialized state, cursor paging, database cleanup on failures, cache restoration after a failed append, and persisted summary totals and labels.
Compaction and session tests assert that retainedTail reconstructs summary plus recent messages and that entries without retainedTail fall back to firstKeptEntryId behavior.
Shared storage tests assert storage-level session statistics include assistant, compaction, and branch-summary usage and assert bounded path behavior for retained-tail compactions.
The node adapter test asserts that the database wrapper supports node:sqlite named parameters.

Repository operations configure WAL, full synchronization, and a busy timeout; apply migrations on open; implement create, open, list, delete, and fork; and close database resources on operation failures or completion.

The checkout contains direct test oracles for schema shape, state round trips, branch reconstruction, transaction rollback, aggregate values, compaction compatibility, and adapter parameter binding, but the evidence bundle does not record an executed test result.
