candidate_workflows.title: Introduce a relational session backend without breaking session semantics
candidate_workflows.description: Extend the storage contract, define a migrated schema, persist event and projection changes atomically, bound context reconstruction at compaction, and validate behavioral parity and failure consistency.

workflow_graph.goal: Provide durable, efficiently queryable session state whose event history, active branch, active leaf, summaries, and reconstructed context remain mutually consistent across create, append, reopen, fork, navigation, and failure.
when_to_use: A new durable backend must implement an existing in-memory or file-backed event-session abstraction.
Resume, listing, statistics, or branch reconstruction requires indexed or materialized state instead of repeatedly scanning the full history.
One logical append updates canonical history and multiple derived representations that must not diverge.
anti_goals: Do not replace the append-only session event model with only a mutable snapshot.
Do not make backend-specific database concepts part of the reusable Session caller API.
Do not silently discard legacy compaction records that lack embedded retained messages.
Do not treat materialized summaries as independently writable sources of truth.
not_applicable_when: The state is intentionally ephemeral and no reopen, fork, listing, or durable recovery behavior is required.
The persisted object has no event history, branching, derived projections, or multi-record consistency boundary.
Existing storage cannot provide a stable typed entry contract or a validation oracle for behavioral parity.
inputs: Existing session entry and repository contracts
Parent implementation behavior for create, append, navigation, fork, context building, and listing
Database adapter with statement and transaction primitives
Ordered schema migrations
Expected derived fields and branch semantics
Shared backend tests and failure-injection tests
workflow_graph.entry_state: Session semantics exist in memory or an append-only file, but the contract assumes full-history access and there is no relational schema or atomic reconciliation of canonical and derived persistent state.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The relational backend satisfies the common session contract; schema versions are recorded; successful operations persist canonical events and matching projections atomically; failed appends restore the prior visible state; reopened sessions preserve metadata, active branch, aggregates, and context; compaction bounds history loading with legacy fallback.

steps.condition: A durable backend cannot efficiently or correctly implement caller-side full-history assumptions.
steps.validation: Compile all storage implementations against the expanded contract and run shared assertions for names, statistics, paths, and paging.

steps.condition: The backend persists related canonical, navigation, ordering, and summary state in a relational database.
steps.validation: Inspect the migration ledger and schema catalog for every required table, column, and index after initialization.

steps.condition: Appending or navigating changes canonical history plus one or more derived representations.
steps.validation: Verify successful metadata, leaf, branch, paging, summary, reopen, and fork round trips; inject a mid-append failure and verify database and local caches remain unchanged.

steps.condition: Context compaction is part of the persisted entry model and loading all pre-compaction ancestors is unnecessary.
steps.validation: Compare context roles and ordering for embedded retained-tail records and legacy boundary-pointer records, and verify branch loading stops at the supported compaction boundary.

validation_ladder: Validate the migration ledger, required tables, active-leaf column, and indexes on a fresh database.
Run common storage behavior checks for metadata, names, aggregate statistics, labels, entry retrieval, and bounded paths.
Exercise create, list, open, append, navigation, fork, paging, and reopen through the relational repository.
Inspect persisted active-leaf, branch-membership, summary, and entry-materialization rows after representative operations.
Inject append and repository failures to verify transaction rollback, process-local state restoration, and database cleanup.
Verify retained-tail and legacy compaction context reconstruction produce the expected message ordering.
Verify the concrete database adapter binds both positional and named parameters.
stop_conditions: Stop if the parent and implementation states cannot establish a stable session behavior contract.
Stop if canonical entries and projections cannot be committed within one atomic persistence boundary.
Stop if reopen or failure-injection tests expose divergence among history, active leaf, branch membership, and summaries.
Defer promotion if only schema creation is tested without behavioral round trips and rollback checks.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence establishes test code but does not include a recorded execution result for the test suite.

The implementation makes firstKeptEntryId optional in the shared CompactionEntry type, but the SQLite entry validator and decoder at this ref still require it to be a string; no test demonstrates SQLite round-trip of a compaction that omits this field.

The materialized-state type includes model-thinking configuration history, but the persisted entry-materialization implementation at this ref stores only label rows, so restoration of that configuration history is not demonstrated.

unresolved_questions: Were the added migration, storage, compaction, session, and adapter tests executed successfully for the pinned commit? The supplied evidence records test sources but no check result.
Should SQLite accept and round-trip a compaction with retainedTail but no firstKeptEntryId? The shared type permits this state, while the SQLite validator and decoder reject it at the pinned ref.
Is persisted restoration of model-thinking configuration history required? The in-memory reducer tracks it, but the pinned entry-materialization code does not serialize or reconstruct those records.

candidate_atomics.name: establish-storage-owned-session-query-contract
candidate_atomics.title: Move persistent session queries behind the storage contract
candidate_atomics.description: Define backend-neutral operations for bounded branch reconstruction, session name and aggregate retrieval, and entry paging so callers do not assume that all state is held in an in-process entry array.

semantic_action.intent: Allow multiple persistence backends to provide equivalent session behavior without forcing callers to scan or load the complete event history.
semantic_action.pre_state: Callers depend on full ancestry traversal, unpaged entry loading, or caller-side scans to derive session information.
semantic_action.post_state: The persistence boundary owns bounded path reconstruction, summary queries, and cursor-based entry retrieval, and Session delegates those operations uniformly.
semantic_action.validation: Run the shared storage and session suites against each backend and verify equivalent names, aggregates, branch paths, and paged entry results.

candidate_atomics.name: persist-event-log-and-derived-state-atomically
candidate_atomics.title: Persist canonical events and derived state in one transaction
candidate_atomics.description: Store the append-only event as the source record while transactionally updating sequence, active leaf, branch membership, and query-oriented materializations; restore process-local state if persistence fails.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent canonical session history, active navigation state, and cached summaries from diverging after partial writes or failures.
semantic_action.pre_state: An append changes several related persistent and in-memory representations whose partial update would expose inconsistent session state.
semantic_action.post_state: A successful append advances all canonical and derived representations together; a failed append leaves both the database and process-local view at the preceding state.
semantic_action.validation: Inject a failure after local caches have been mutated and assert no entry or leaf change remains; separately inspect persisted summary, active-leaf, and branch rows after successful appends.

candidate_atomics.name: apply-versioned-persistence-schema
candidate_atomics.title: Initialize persistent storage through recorded migrations
candidate_atomics.description: Create the relational state model through ordered, idempotent migration files recorded in a migration ledger rather than relying on ad hoc table creation.

semantic_action.intent: Make persistent schema initialization repeatable and observable across database opens and future schema evolution.
semantic_action.pre_state: The database may be absent or may have only a subset of known schema migrations applied.
semantic_action.post_state: Every known unapplied migration has run transactionally once, its identifier is recorded, and the required tables and indexes exist.
semantic_action.validation: Open a new database, inspect the migration ledger and schema catalog, then reopen it and verify already-recorded migrations are skipped without schema duplication.

candidate_atomics.name: bound-context-reconstruction-at-compaction
candidate_atomics.title: Make compaction entries self-contained for recent context
candidate_atomics.description: Persist the messages retained by compaction directly on the compaction record and stop branch loading there, while preserving an older boundary-pointer fallback.

semantic_action.intent: Reconstruct current model context without loading irrelevant ancestors before the latest compaction while continuing to read older persisted sessions.
semantic_action.pre_state: A compaction summary points to the first retained ancestor, requiring ancestry traversal to recover recent messages; older records contain only that pointer.
semantic_action.post_state: New compactions contain their retained recent messages and terminate ancestry loading; legacy compactions still reconstruct context from the retained-entry boundary.
semantic_action.validation: Assert that a retained-tail compaction produces summary plus its stored recent messages and post-compaction messages, and that a legacy compaction produces the same logical ordering through firstKeptEntryId fallback.

title: Keep session state available under SQLite contention and reconcile incomplete transcript migration
before: At parent commit 3a7907b278169110d4fe16e1d50cb316ad5944e0, SQLite connections waited 10 seconds for locks; duplicate session creation used a strict INSERT; an initialization failure discarded the agent's database handle for its remaining lifetime; message flushes assumed the parent session row already existed; message search held one lock while performing every context query; and transcript loading returned any non-empty SQLite result without checking whether legacy JSONL contained a longer history.
after: At b81d49dc450a56791a4ba39401f785eaff573d59, connections wait 30 seconds, session creation is first-write-wins and idempotent, transient initialization failure no longer disables the database handle, every flush idempotently ensures the session row before appending messages, search context queries use separate short lock acquisitions, and transcript loading reads both SQLite and JSONL then chooses the longer source, preferring SQLite on equal counts.
diff: The commit modifies gateway/session.py, hermes_state.py, and run_agent.py and adds regression coverage in tests/gateway/test_session.py and tests/test_hermes_state.py. The implementation changes strict session insertion to INSERT OR IGNORE, adds ensure_session and invokes it at the flush boundary, preserves the database object after create_session errors, increases the SQLite busy timeout, narrows search lock scope, and replaces SQLite-first early return with length-based reconciliation of dual transcript stores. The targeted added test classes execute successfully: 10 tests passed.

commit.subject: fix(state): SQLite concurrency hardening + session transcript integrity (#3249)
commit.body_excerpt:
* fix(session-db): survive CLI/gateway concurrent write contention

Closes #3139

Three layered fixes for the scenario where CLI and gateway write to
state.db concurrently, causing create_session() to fail with
'database is locked' and permanently disabling session_search on the
gateway side.

1. Increase SQLite connection timeout: 10s -> 30s
   hermes_state.py: longer window for the WAL writer to finish a batch
   flush before the other process gives up entirely.

2. INSERT OR IGNORE in create_session
   hermes_state.py: prevents IntegrityError on duplicate session IDs
   (e.g. gateway restarts while CLI session is still alive).

3. Don't null out _session_db on create_session failure  (main fix)
   run_agent.py: a transient lock at agent startup must not permanently
   disable session_search for the lifetime of that agent instance.
   _session_db now stays alive so subsequent flushes and searches work
   once the lock clears.

4. New ensure_session() helper + call it during flush
   hermes_state.py: INSERT OR IGNORE for a minimal session row.
   run_agent.py _flush_messages_to_session_db: calls ensure_session()
   before appending messages, so the FK constraint is satisfied even

    fix(state): SQLite concurrency hardening + session transcript integrity (#3249)
    
    * fix(session-db): survive CLI/gateway concurrent write contention
    
    Closes #3139
    
    Three layered fixes for the scenario where CLI and gateway write to
    state.db concurrently, causing create_session() to fail with
    'database is locked' and permanently disabling session_search on the
    gateway side.
    
    1. Increase SQLite connection timeout: 10s -> 30s
       hermes_state.py: longer window for the WAL writer to finish a batch
       flush before the other process gives up entirely.
    
    2. INSERT OR IGNORE in create_session
       hermes_state.py: prevents IntegrityError on duplicate session IDs
       (e.g. gateway restarts while CLI session is still alive).
    
    3. Don't null out _session_db on create_session failure  (main fix)
       run_agent.py: a transient lock at agent startup must not permanently
       disable session_search for the lifetime of that agent instance.
       _session_db now stays alive so subsequent flushes and searches work
       once the lock clears.
    
    4. New ensure_session() helper + call it during flush
       hermes_state.py: INSERT OR IGNORE for a minimal session row.
       run_agent.py _flush_messages_to_session_db: calls ensure_session()
       before appending messages, so the FK constraint is satisfied even
       when create_session() failed at startup. No-op when the row exists.
    
    * fix(state): release lock between context queries in search_messages
    
    The context-window queries (one per FTS5 match) were running inside
    the same lock acquisition as the primary FTS5 query, holding the lock
    for O(N) sequential SQLite round-trips. Move per-match context fetches
    outside the outer lock block so each acquires the lock independently,
    keeping critical sections short and allowing other threads to interleave.
    
    * fix(session): prefer longer source in load_transcript to prevent legacy truncation
    
    When a long-lived session pre-dates SQLite storage (e.g. sessions
    created before the DB layer was introduced, or after a clean
    deployment that reset the DB), _flush_messages_to_session_db only
    writes the *new* messages from the current turn to SQLite — it skips
    messages already present in conversation_history, assuming they are
    already persisted.
    
    That assumption fails for legacy JSONL-only sessions:
    
      Turn N (first after DB migration):
        load_transcript(id)       → SQLite: 0  → falls back to JSONL: 994 ✓
        _flush_messages_to_session_db: skip first 994, write 2 new → SQLite: 2
    
      Turn N+1:
        load_transcript(id)       → SQLite: 2  → returns immediately ✗
        Agent sees 2 messages of history instead of 996
    
    The same pattern causes the reported symptom: session JSON truncated
    to 4 messages (_save_session_log writes agent.messages which only has
    2 history + 2 new = 4).
    
    Fix: always load both sources and return whichever is longer.  For a
    fully-migrated session SQLite will always be ≥ JSONL, so there is no
    regression.  For a legacy session that hasn't been bootstrapped yet,
    JSONL wins and the full history is restored.
    
    Closes #3212
    
    * test: add load_transcript source preference tests for #3212
    
    Covers: JSONL longer returns JSONL, SQLite longer returns SQLite,
    SQLite empty falls back to JSONL, both empty returns empty, equal
    length prefers SQLite (richer reasoning fields).

candidate_atomics.name: make-session-row-creation-idempotent
candidate_atomics.title: Make session-row creation safe to repeat
candidate_atomics.description: Use first-write-wins insertion for stable session identifiers so concurrent components or restarts can request the same parent row without raising or overwriting established metadata.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent duplicate session identifiers from turning normal concurrent or restart behavior into a persistence failure.
semantic_action.pre_state: Creating an already-present session identifier executes a strict insert and can raise an integrity error.
semantic_action.post_state: Creating the same identifier repeatedly succeeds, leaves one session row, and retains the metadata from the first successful creation.
semantic_action.validation: Create the same identifier twice with different metadata and verify no exception occurs and the stored row still contains the first write.

candidate_atomics.name: repair-missing-session-parent-before-flush
candidate_atomics.title: Repair a missing session parent before appending messages
candidate_atomics.description: At the persistence boundary, idempotently establish the minimal parent record required by message foreign keys before appending new conversation rows.

semantic_action.intent: Allow later persistence to recover when initial session registration failed transiently.
semantic_action.pre_state: The database handle is usable but the active session row may be absent, so appending child messages can violate the parent-row requirement.
semantic_action.post_state: A minimal parent session row exists before message appends, while any pre-existing row remains unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Verify missing-row creation, existing-row no-op behavior, and successful message append after late parent creation.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-persistence-capability-after-transient-init-failure
candidate_atomics.title: Keep persistence available after transient initialization failure
candidate_atomics.description: Retain the initialized storage object when initial session registration fails so later flushes and searches can retry after contention clears.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a transient startup error from disabling persistent session features for the entire agent lifetime.
semantic_action.pre_state: An exception during initial session-row creation causes the live database handle to be discarded.
semantic_action.post_state: The database handle remains available after registration failure, allowing later operations to recover through normal persistence boundaries.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the exception path to confirm it reports failure without clearing the handle, then validate the downstream flush repair operation independently.

candidate_atomics.name: bound-sqlite-contention-wait
candidate_atomics.title: Give concurrent writers a bounded recovery window
candidate_atomics.description: Increase the connection-level busy timeout so short-lived write ownership by another process can clear before an operation fails.

semantic_action.intent: Reduce avoidable lock failures during concurrent writes without introducing unbounded waiting.

title: Consolidate dynamic-tool persistence onto rollout session metadata while retaining schema compatibility
before: At parent commit 0db49a7e6ae8fd459dd8d8d404086c748b9118a1, thread-start dynamic tools had two persistence paths. Rollout SessionMeta stored them, while SQLite also copied them into thread_dynamic_tools through incremental rollout application, rollout backfill/reconciliation, and thread-metadata synchronization. When a resumed or forked session supplied no tools directly, session initialization queried SQLite first and only then fell back to rollout history.
after: At commit 304d15cab0b1c5f23925e5a3b94c39db3483fc3d, rollout session metadata is the sole active persistence and restoration path for thread-start dynamic tools. Session initialization obtains missing tools directly from conversation history even when SQLite is enabled; SQLite reads, writes, backfill/reconciliation, and metadata-patch propagation for dynamic tools are removed. The existing thread_dynamic_tools table and migrations remain intact for older-binary compatibility.
diff: The change modifies nine Rust files with 101 insertions and 260 deletions. It simplifies session initialization from a database-first/fallback lookup to conversation_history.get_dynamic_tools(), deletes dynamic-tool database APIs and extraction logic, removes dynamic_tools from ThreadMetadataPatch and synchronization paths, removes the backfill assertion that tools are copied into SQLite, and adds an SQLite-enabled resume integration test that starts a thread with a tool, resumes from its rollout, and verifies the restored tool name, description, and input schema in the next request.

commit.subject: [codex] Remove redundant SQLite dynamic tool storage (#24819)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

Dynamic tools are defined at thread start and already stored in rollout
`SessionMeta`, which restores resumed and forked sessions. Persisting
the same tools through SQLite creates a second runtime persistence path
that is unnecessary prework for the explicit namespace refactor.

## What changed

- Restore missing thread-start dynamic tools directly from rollout
history, including when SQLite is enabled.
- Remove SQLite dynamic-tool reads, writes, backfill, and thread
metadata patch plumbing.
- Add SQLite-enabled resume integration coverage that verifies a
rollout-defined dynamic tool is still sent after resume.

## Compatibility

The existing `thread_dynamic_tools` table is intentionally not dropped
even though it's now unused. Older Codex binaries are allowed to open
databases migrated by newer binaries and still reference this table;
dropping it would break that mixed-version path. See
[here](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/state/src/migrations.rs#L10-L11).

## Verification

- `just test -p codex-state -p codex-rollout -p codex-thread-store`
- `just test -p codex-core --test all
resume_restores_dynamic_tools_from_rollout_with_sqlite_enabled`

candidate_workflows.title: Consolidate duplicated persistent state without breaking restoration or older schemas
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for replacing two active persistence paths with one authoritative history source, removing the redundant replica end to end, preserving compatibility-sensitive schema, and proving behavior at the resume boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Make one persisted history record authoritative for immutable session configuration, eliminate the secondary runtime replica, and retain any schema required for mixed-version compatibility while preserving resume behavior.
when_to_use: The same immutable or thread-start state is persisted in both an authoritative event/history record and a secondary database representation.

title: Serialize policy persistence and validate stored regular-expression rules
before: At parent be2ebd1772e3562f4caf535067bb2d0e071ae6b8, every persistent policy-update event independently read, modified, and wrote the same auto-saved TOML file. All writes shared one fixed `<policyFile>.tmp` staging path and used a non-exclusive write, so overlapping events could read stale state, lose one another's rules, or race while renaming the same temporary file. Raw `argsPattern` values were also compiled and admitted without length or nested-quantifier safety checks.
after: At 6d3fff2ea445c18348c76feb72f524f2b685be21, one promise queue per policy updater serializes persistent read-modify-write operations. Each operation stages serialized TOML in a random-suffixed temporary file opened exclusively with `wx`, closes its handle, and atomically renames it to the target. A shared regular-expression validator rejects invalid, overlong, and nested-quantifier patterns before dynamic rule admission and while loading persisted policy and safety-checker rules.
diff: The change imports cryptographic randomness and a new regex-safety helper; adds a sequential persistence promise chain; replaces the fixed temporary pathname and direct `writeFile` with a random temporary pathname, exclusive file creation, handle-based writing and closing, then rename; validates raw regex patterns at both update and TOML-load boundaries; and updates tests for exclusive staging plus tests for unsafe-pattern rejection. Six policy implementation/test files changed.

episode.title: Serialize policy persistence and validate stored regular-expression rules
episode.before: At parent be2ebd1772e3562f4caf535067bb2d0e071ae6b8, every persistent policy-update event independently read, modified, and wrote the same auto-saved TOML file. All writes shared one fixed `<policyFile>.tmp` staging path and used a non-exclusive write, so overlapping events could read stale state, lose one another's rules, or race while renaming the same temporary file. Raw `argsPattern` values were also compiled and admitted without length or nested-quantifier safety checks.
episode.after: At 6d3fff2ea445c18348c76feb72f524f2b685be21, one promise queue per policy updater serializes persistent read-modify-write operations. Each operation stages serialized TOML in a random-suffixed temporary file opened exclusively with `wx`, closes its handle, and atomically renames it to the target. A shared regular-expression validator rejects invalid, overlong, and nested-quantifier patterns before dynamic rule admission and while loading persisted policy and safety-checker rules.
episode.diff: The change imports cryptographic randomness and a new regex-safety helper; adds a sequential persistence promise chain; replaces the fixed temporary pathname and direct `writeFile` with a random temporary pathname, exclusive file creation, handle-based writing and closing, then rename; validates raw regex patterns at both update and TOML-load boundaries; and updates tests for exclusive staging plus tests for unsafe-pattern rejection. Six policy implementation/test files changed.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 6d3fff2ea445c18348c76feb72f524f2b685be21 has parent be2ebd1772e3562f4caf535067bb2d0e071ae6b8 and subject `fix(core): prevent race condition in policy persistence (#18506)`.

The parent implementation performed each persistent event's read-modify-write directly, used the shared path `${policyFile}.tmp`, wrote it with `fs.writeFile`, and renamed it to the policy file without a serialization queue.

The updated policy updater creates a promise-based persistence queue and appends each persistent read-modify-write operation to that queue, preventing overlapping operations within one updater instance.

Each queued write now uses an eight-byte random hexadecimal suffix, opens the temporary file with exclusive `wx` semantics, writes through the returned handle, closes it in a finally block, and renames it to the stable policy pathname.
Persistent behavior is entered through the UPDATE_POLICY message subscriber only when the incoming message has `persist` enabled; non-persistent updates still modify only the in-memory policy engine.

Persistence tests publish UPDATE_POLICY messages and assert that the implementation opens a `.tmp` path with `wx`, writes the expected TOML through the file handle, and renames the staging file to `auto-saved.toml`; command-prefix and provider-qualified rule representations remain covered.
The new regex validator first checks compilation, rejects patterns longer than 2048 characters, and heuristically rejects groups containing a quantifier that are themselves quantified.
Dynamic policy updates reject an unsafe raw args pattern before adding an in-memory rule or reaching persistence, while command-prefix patterns continue through the escaped pattern builder.

The TOML loader applies the same safety predicate to persisted policy rules and safety-checker rules, records a regex-compilation error for unsafe patterns, and excludes those entries from the loaded rule sets.
Unit tests accept representative simple, quantified, and grouped patterns and reject malformed, 2049-character, and nested-quantifier patterns.
The policy-updater test publishes an update containing `(a+)+` and verifies that no policy rule is added.
The commit changed the policy updater, persistence tests, updater tests, TOML loader, regex utility, and regex utility tests.

The checked-in tests provide direct oracles for exclusive temporary-file creation, serialized TOML content, atomic rename invocation, regex classification, and rejection at the live update boundary; the commit does not add a test that drives two persistent updates concurrently.

candidate_atomics.name: serialize_persistent_read_modify_write
candidate_atomics.title: Serialize persistent read-modify-write updates
candidate_atomics.description: Route state-changing persistence requests through a per-owner promise chain so each operation observes the result of the preceding operation before reading and appending state.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent concurrent persistence events in one process from losing previously accepted state through overlapping reads and writes.
semantic_action.pre_state: Multiple accepted persistence events can independently enter the same read-parse-append-write sequence against one state file.
semantic_action.post_state: Each persistence operation starts only after the preceding queued operation has completed, so later reads can observe earlier committed updates.
semantic_action.validation: Publish multiple persistent updates without awaiting individual listener completion, then verify the final parsed state contains every rule in queue order and no persistence-error feedback was emitted. The implementation establishes the queue, but this exact concurrent oracle is not present in the changed tests.

candidate_atomics.name: isolate_atomic_write_staging
candidate_atomics.title: Give each atomic write an exclusive staging file
candidate_atomics.description: Create a unique temporary file exclusively, write and close it, then rename it over the stable state file so writers do not contend for one shared staging pathname.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent temporary-file collisions and incomplete replacement during persistent state writes.
semantic_action.pre_state: Writers share one predictable temporary pathname and create or truncate it through a non-exclusive write.
semantic_action.post_state: Each write owns a newly created unique staging file, closes it after complete serialization, and replaces the stable target through rename.
semantic_action.validation: Assert the staging pathname ends in `.tmp`, is opened with `wx`, receives the serialized state through its handle, is closed, and is renamed to the stable target; exercise two writers to verify distinct staging names.

candidate_atomics.name: validate_regex_state_at_ingress
candidate_atomics.title: Reject unsafe regular expressions at every state-ingress boundary
candidate_atomics.description: Apply one bounded regex-safety predicate before admitting live updates and before reconstructing runtime objects from persisted configuration.

Test the live update boundary to prove a rejected expression cannot mutate active state.
Test serialization content and the exclusive staging-file/open/write/rename protocol.

stop_conditions: Stop if the updater cannot identify one stable state target or cannot scope a serialization owner around all same-process writers.
Stop if expression-bearing inputs cannot be identified before compilation or persistence.
Do not claim multi-process lost-update prevention from unique staging files alone; the queue is local to one updater instance.

candidate_atomics.name: serialize_persistent_read_modify_write
candidate_atomics.title: Serialize persistent read-modify-write updates
candidate_atomics.description: Route state-changing persistence requests through a per-owner promise chain so each operation observes the result of the preceding operation before reading and appending state.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent concurrent persistence events in one process from losing previously accepted state through overlapping reads and writes.
semantic_action.pre_state: Multiple accepted persistence events can independently enter the same read-parse-append-write sequence against one state file.
semantic_action.post_state: Each persistence operation starts only after the preceding queued operation has completed, so later reads can observe earlier committed updates.
semantic_action.validation: Publish multiple persistent updates without awaiting individual listener completion, then verify the final parsed state contains every rule in queue order and no persistence-error feedback was emitted. The implementation establishes the queue, but this exact concurrent oracle is not present in the changed tests.

candidate_atomics.name: isolate_atomic_write_staging
candidate_atomics.title: Give each atomic write an exclusive staging file
candidate_atomics.description: Create a unique temporary file exclusively, write and close it, then rename it over the stable state file so writers do not contend for one shared staging pathname.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent temporary-file collisions and incomplete replacement during persistent state writes.
semantic_action.pre_state: Writers share one predictable temporary pathname and create or truncate it through a non-exclusive write.
semantic_action.post_state: Each write owns a newly created unique staging file, closes it after complete serialization, and replaces the stable target through rename.
semantic_action.validation: Assert the staging pathname ends in `.tmp`, is opened with `wx`, receives the serialized state through its handle, is closed, and is renamed to the stable target; exercise two writers to verify distinct staging names.

call_sites: Persistent behavior is entered through the UPDATE_POLICY message subscriber only when the incoming message has `persist` enabled; non-persistent updates still modify only the in-memory policy engine.
tests: Persistence tests publish UPDATE_POLICY messages and assert that the implementation opens a `.tmp` path with `wx`, writes the expected TOML through the file handle, and renames the staging file to `auto-saved.toml`; command-prefix and provider-qualified rule representations remain covered.
Unit tests accept representative simple, quantified, and grouped patterns and reject malformed, 2049-character, and nested-quantifier patterns.
The policy-updater test publishes an update containing `(a+)+` and verifies that no policy rule is added.
